626cafd438c63b42: KUALA LUMPUR: Datuk Seri Najib Razak has failed in his bid to stay his 15-year jail sentence and RM11.4 billion fine in the 1Malaysia Development Bhd (1MDB) case pending his appeal.
High Court judge Noor Ruwena Md Nurdin dismissed the former prime minister's application today after hearing submissions from the defence and prosecution.

Najib, 73, had sought the stay on several grounds, including his deteriorating health and the total fines of approximately RM13.47 billion imposed on him for the offences, while the prosecution argued that he had failed to establish special or exceptional circumstances to justify the application.

On Dec 26 last year, Najib was convicted of four counts of abuse of power and 21 counts of money laundering involving RM2.27 billion in 1MDB funds. He was sentenced to 15 years' imprisonment and fined approximately RM13.47 billion.

The prison sentences were ordered to run concurrently but would only begin after he completed his existing sentence in the SRC International case. Najib has appealed against both his conviction and sentence.
c9b6a2eb32a3c606: KUALA LUMPUR: His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, attended the 273rd Conference of Rulers meeting at Istana Negara, chaired by the Sultan of Perak, Sultan Nazrin Muizzuddin Shah.

The Regent of Terengganu, Tengku Muhammad Ismail Sultan Mizan Zainal Abidin; Crown Prince of Kelantan, Tengku Muhammad Fakhry Petra; and Tunku Temenggong of Johor, Tunku Idris Iskandar Sultan Ibrahim, also attended.

b116934e517209ef: TOKYO: Japan's prime minister said on Wednesday she probably spends "three or four more hours" than her male predecessors tackling household duties on top of her already packed daily schedule.
"In the morning, I bathe, fix breakfast and then wash dishes, not to mention apply makeup," Sanae Takaichi, elected last year as Japan's first woman premier, told parliament.
"I feel like I'm spending three or four more hours than male prime ministers doing these things."
A self-described workaholic, Takaichi has previously said she slept just two to four hours a night and sometimes scheduled 3am staff meetings.

Gender roles are rigid in Japan and women are chronically under-represented in politics, with just 68 women lawmakers elected out of 465 seats up for grabs at the last lower house election in February.
Discussions about Takaichi's time management came up when a ruling coalition member asked her about the marathon hours Japanese prime ministers customarily spend attending parliamentary sessions.
It is common for Japanese leaders to devote five to seven hours a day being grilled by opposition lawmakers or otherwise just sitting in parliament.

Citing a study, lawmaker Fumitake Fujita of the Japan Innovation Party said that, in 2022, Japan's prime minister attended parliamentary sessions for 72 days, versus 50 days in the United Kingdom and 13 in Germany.
While acknowledging the importance of legislative discussions, Fujita said: "The fact that our leader is confined for such long hours to parliament isn't in line with the global standards."
Takaichi said in a post on X in July that she was "getting consumed until dawn with poring over documents brought home from work and those related to parliamentary questioning."
"I do enjoy reading these piles of documents at midnight that I took home," she said on Wednesday.
"But it is difficult for me to squeeze out time to buckle down and think with a clear head" about "the future direction of this country or my grand vision for it", she said.
5252753164f8fd0e: WUHAN, Oct 14 — Six-time Grand Slam champion Iga Swiatek launched her Wuhan Open campaign by triumphing 6-2, 6-1 in an all-Polish battle against lucky loser Magdalena Frech today.
Swiatek posted her 40th victory of the season in one hour and 42 minutes and remains on course for a potential quarter-final showdown with top seed and three-time Wuhan winner Aryna Sabalenka.
“We know each other pretty well, so I just wanted to focus on being consistent and playing as good as possible,” Swiatek, the seventh seed, said of Frech.
Poland’s Magdalena Frech hits a return to Poland’s Iga Swiatek during their women’s singles match at the Wuhan Open tennis tournament in Wuhan, China’s Hubei province October 14, 2026. — AFP pic

“I know she is running to every ball always and sometimes using the power of the opponent, so I wanted to not play too crazy but play solid and I’m happy that I did that,” said Swiatek, who is chasing a qualification spot for the year-end WTA Finals.

Despite the lopsided scoreline the opening set was tight, lasting over an hour and requiring Swiatek to erase a 0-2 deficit and save seven of eight break points before she finally took the lead on her fourth set point.
Upping the pressure with her relentless forehand, Swiatek claimed a 10th game in a row to build a 4-0 advantage in the second set.
The former world number one briefly lost momentum, getting broken by Frech, but recovered to advance to the round of 16, where she awaits one of two lucky losers, Lanlana Tararudee or Ashlyn Krueger.

British world number 170 Sonay Kartal, who missed six months this year with a spinal stress fracture, upset ninth-seeded Belinda Bencic 6-0, 7-5 to book a date with Jasmine Paolini or Nikola Bartunkova. — AFP
cfd6d461206fc42e: KUALA LUMPUR: National sepak takraw squad head coach Ahmad Jais Baharun is resigned to the fact that one of his key players - Noraizat Nordin - could miss next year's Malaysia SEA Games due to a long-term injury.

Jais confirmed that Noraizat, who was sidelined for the recent Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games, will have to go under the surgeon's knife to help him recover from an anterior cruciate ligament injury in his right knee.

"We are working closely with the National Sports Institute (NSI) in managing Noraizat's injury. The doctors from NSI will advise where it is best for Noraizat to get the surgery done. We do not want to take too long before the surgery is done," said Jais yesterday.
"Once he has done the surgery, the recovery process will take a long time, at least six months before he can return to training. It could take longer.
"There are a lot of factors to consider, this includes his own desire and determination to come back from the injury.
"So if it does take six months, he will be left with only five months before the Malaysia SEA Games (Sept 18-27)."
Jais said he has to be prepared with a plan if Noraizat is unable to return to full fitness in time for the Games.
"We have to plan effectively, in case his recovery takes longer than expected. We have to have a plan A and a plan B," he said.
"We have to determine who can replace him if he cannot make the squad, especially in the doubles event.
"This is something we have to discuss together with the Malaysia Sepak Takraw Federation, National Sports Council and NSI."
Noraizat, who plays in the killer position, was part of the squad that won the men's team event gold at the Thailand SEA Games last year.
He also won the men's doubles gold with partner Aidil Aiman Azwawi during the 2024 World Cup, when they beat Thailand in the final.
fe97da165e53b3e2: JOHOR BARU: Pasir Gudang recorded the country's highest Air Pollutant Index (API) reading of 180, placing it in the unhealthy category as haze continued to affect Johor.
The latest readings showed that all seven other monitoring stations in the state, except Segamat, also recorded unhealthy air quality, with readings ranging from 152 to 170.
Pengerang recorded an API reading of 170, followed by Larkin (169), Kota Tinggi (168), Batu Pahat (154), Kluang (153) and Tangkak (152).
Segamat was the only monitoring station in Johor to record moderate air quality, with an API reading of 95.
Fine particulate matter (PM2.5) was the dominant pollutant at all eight monitoring stations.
An API reading of between 101 and 200 is classified as unhealthy, while readings between 51 and 100 are considered moderate.
568e5b36cd1ab8ec: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 14 — Bank Negara Malaysia (BNM) and the Securities Commission Malaysia (SC) have warned the public against deepfake videos impersonating their senior officers to promote private investment schemes and financial products.

In a statement, BNM said members of the public who encounter suspicious content were urged to report it to the relevant social media platform or alert BNM or the SC to help prevent its further spread.
BNM said the public could visit its official website at bnm.gov.my/verify for examples of deepfake content and impersonation involving the central bank.
The public was also advised to check BNM’s Financial Consumer Alert List and the SC’s Investor Alert List for entities or schemes flagged by the authorities.
“Verify whether the entity is authorised to offer financial or investment products through BNMLINK or the SC’s Investment Checker portal,” it said.
BNM also encouraged the public to follow the Amaran Scam Facebook page for updates on emerging scams and tips to avoid falling victim to fraudulent activities. — Bernama
f4cd9013caf51b22: Why are we in such a hurry? Are we in a race? Where's the finish line? Are we in the lead? Far behind? I increasingly hear these questions about AI from people who feel a gritty sense of being unpleasantly overstimulated – like a three-year-old allowed to stay awake too long and now unable to sleep. That feeling has become worse since last November when AI tools suddenly became "good enough" to be broadly useful. A whole cohort of engineers – myself included – found themselves infused with manic energy, bursting with ideas on how to prompt up tools and processes with this wonderful new toy. Usage exploded – as has revenue. The AI firms, finally on a path to something vaguely suggestive of profitability, leaned in and increased their release cadence. Every new model felt like Christmas. We've had a lot of Christmases these past ten months or so. Almost every engineer I know has accrued a massive "toy debt," unable to stop experimenting with more tools than any of us could ever hope to master across an entire career. Each new model delivers a quick dopamine hit to users, but the high wears off and the slump arrives. That's where we are now. Engineers feel exhausted. The race to "Super Intelligence" (whatever that is) left us with something else entirely: call it "stupor intelligence" – the feeling that we've absorbed more than we can digest. More AI would just be pointless excess. If that's the view from inside the AI bubble, how does it look on the outside? Not so great. The Wall Street Journal confidently reports that 63 percent of Americans favor an immediate pause or slowdown in AI development. They can see this technology is moving too fast, in too manic a rush, and without control. It's making them uneasy. That shapeless unease takes form as a widespread anxiety that the machines will soon rise up to kill us all. It's reflected within the industry as people spectacularly burn out, posting long screeds about the imminent human extinction event. Former Anthropic staffer Jacob Coxon's resignation post went viral because it gave folks a focus for their anxieties. Would it kill us to pause and catch our breath? Here's the raw truth: businesses already have more technological change to digest than they can work through for years to come. We've a wealth of "good enough" AI – American, Chinese, and European – to completely transform business operations. That will happen, but on a timescale of years, not days. Bringing new, better, shinier AI models to market has become a project of diminishing returns. Not because the models have plateaued, but because the culture has. We simply can't process any more AI. So how do we stop? The profitable loop between the model makers and their customers won't pause on its own. It will only go faster and harder. At the same time, we're seeing the stirrings of a Luddite 2.0 movement, intent on destroying the machines before they replace all the workers. Resistance to datacenters is the friendly face of something that could turn ugly if we simply keep charging ahead. One thing could slow us: the cost of keeping these systems under control. The smarter models become, the more difficult they are to manage. Every day brings more reports of "rogue agents" reaching external systems from labs that seem to have avoided the hard work of designing secure test environments. More powerful models could prove increasingly costly to contain. Eventually, costs outweigh benefits. We could be one lawsuit away from reaching a pause, when the frontier labs and their products become uninsurable risks. Here's hoping we pause before some real mischief occurs. Otherwise, plugs may be pulled, and all the pretty Christmas lights will go out. Better by far to act with agency, clear-eyed and humble, than confront force majeure. ®

165167354d571fc3: BATU PAHAT: A single mother was fined RM1,000 by the magistrate's court here today for lodging a false police report claiming she had been robbed to avoid paying the fee to replace her lost MyKad.
Magistrate Mustaqim Sukarno imposed the fine on Keranjeet Kaur Shivinder, 41, after she pleaded guilty. She paid the fine, in default of which she would have faced five months' jail.
Keranjeet, a mother of two, was charged with falsely claiming that two men on a motorcycle had snatched her handbag in Kampung Jorak Elahi, Bukit Pasir, on Sept 12.
She lodged the report at the Cyberjaya police station in Sepang, Selangor, at 12.37pm on Sept 15.
She was charged under Section 182 of the Penal Code, which provides for a jail term of up to six months, a fine of up to RM2,000, or both, upon conviction.
In her report, Keranjeet claimed the incident occurred at 11.20pm on Sept 12, with her handbag containing her identity card, bank cards, house keys and RM210 in cash.
Police opened an investigation but, during questioning on Sept 18, she admitted that the robbery had never taken place.
She said she had fabricated the incident because she had misplaced her identity card and wanted to obtain a replacement without paying the required fee.
Deputy public prosecutor Nur Shahzleen Ibrahim prosecuted, while Keranjeet was represented by Normaahani Rais of the National Legal Aid Foundation.
2b7db460b89b1303: SEOUL, Oct 14 — South Korean running influencer and artificial intelligence semiconductor researcher Yoo Ji-won has died after collapsing during the 2026 Seoul Race, according to Resonate Voices.
She was 25 years old and was a graduate student at the Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology (KAIST).
Yoo lost consciousness at the 20.6-kilometre mark of the 21-kilometre half-marathon course, roughly 500 metres from the finish line.
“At around 8.49am on October 11, an emergency situation occurred when a participant in the half course collapsed at the 20.6km mark,” the organising committee stated.
“After immediate first aid on site, the participant was transported to a medical facility by 119 ambulance for treatment, but unfortunately, passed away.”
Medical authorities have not confirmed an official cause of death.
The Seoul Race Organising Committee confirmed the fatality in an official statement to participants on Monday and extended its support to her family as investigations continue.
View this post on Instagram
“We respectfully pray for the deceased’s peaceful rest and extend our deepest sympathies to the bereaved family facing this sudden sorrow,” the statement added.
“We will carefully examine this incident and proceed with necessary follow-up measures without fail.”
Yoo, who was born in 2001, earned wide admiration in South Korean running circles for combining elite athletic endurance with demanding scientific research at KAIST.
She began distance running in 2022 and cultivated a devoted online following by documenting her training alongside her laboratory work on next-generation computing hardware.
Her performances established her among the country’s leading amateur long-distance runners.
On March 15, 2026, Yoo finished the full Seoul Marathon in two hours, 56 minutes and 32 seconds.
View this post on Instagram
That result secured her a “sub-3” marathon finish — a highly prized standard achieved by very few non-professional runners.
She had earlier claimed victory in the women’s masters 10-kilometre category at the Gunsan Saemangeum Marathon in the spring.
After her collapse, false claims spread on social media suggesting hospital staff had treated and released her to recover at home.
Friends and running partners stepped in online to set the record straight and appealed for privacy for her family.
“Jiwon continued to be hospitalised after collapsing, and she continued to have a hard time without ever being discharged,” one acquaintance wrote on social media.
The friend urged fellow runners to focus on honouring her memory and praying for her family instead of circulating unverified information.
Since then, tributes have poured onto Yoo’s social media accounts from club runners, engineers and athletics fans throughout South Korea.
81870d47723caf95: KUALA LUMPUR: Protecting access to fisheries and offshore resources in the South China Sea requires stronger maritime capabilities, while growing military activity in the area could increase the risk of miscalculation, potentially leading to incidents that disrupt sea lanes, a conference heard.
Security analyst and retired US Navy Captain Brent Sadler said countries could no longer rely on legal frameworks and arbitration alone to safeguard their interests.
International Tribunal for the Law of the Sea (ITLOS) judge Dr Nguyen Thi Lan Anh called for legal clarity and cooperation to reduce maritime risks.
They were speaking during the first panel session of the ninth MIMA South China Sea Conference 2026 themed "South China Sea 2026: Rules, Resilience, and Regional Order" on Tuesday.

Sadler, a senior research fellow in naval warfare and advanced technology at The Heritage Foundation's Allison Centre for National Security in the US, urged countries to clearly define their national interests and strengthen their ability to defend those interests at sea.
"There's the language of diplomacy, there's the language of economics, but there's also the language of action, and that's the military and what military and paramilitary forces do," he said.
He also proposed that South China Sea claimant states work together to establish standards of behaviour and communicate their expectations to other countries, including the US.
"Peace can be assured, but it's not going to be easy to maintain, and it's going to require all sides to be active in that regard," he said.

Meanwhile, Nguyen warned that an increasing military presence and differing interpretations of maritime rules could heighten the risk of misunderstanding and miscalculation, potentially disrupting sea lanes.

She said a proper application of the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS) requires clarity on where an incident occurred, which navigational regime applied, the vessel or aircraft involved, and the activities being conducted.
Navigational rights differ across territorial waters, international straits, exclusive economic zones (EEZs) and the high seas, she said.

In an EEZ, freedom of navigation has to be exercised with due regard for the coastal state's sovereign rights and jurisdiction, while coastal states must also avoid abusing their jurisdiction to hinder lawful navigation.
Nguyen called for data and information sharing to build a common understanding of maritime risks and help countries cooperate in addressing them.
She said the maritime security agenda also extends to undersea cables, energy pipelines, and unmanned vessels, and requires attention to how existing rules apply to emerging technologies.
"The third party objective method or forum always can be helpful," she said, and highlighted advisory opinions and provisional measures alongside dispute settlement mechanisms.

Citing Malaysia and Singapore's use of arbitration and ITLOS provisional measures before reaching a negotiated settlement, Nguyen said legal mechanisms could help countries resolve differences and promote cooperation without prejudice to their positions on sovereignty or maritime disputes.

Hosted by the Maritime Institute of Malaysia (MIMA), the Oct 13 and 14 conference brings together policymakers, diplomats, academics, and maritime security experts to examine regional cooperation, resilience, and maritime legal frameworks.

6ddaf644bbec5e8b: KUALA LUMPUR: Olympic champion An Se Young jokingly entertained the idea of playing women's doubles after cruising into the second round of the Denmark Open in Odense today.
South Korean badminton superstar defeated Ukraine's world No. 41 Polina Buhrova 21-13, 21-11.
In a lighthearted Badminton World Federation interview following the match, a reporter asked if she would consider playing men's singles given her dominance in the women's game.
"What are you talking about? No, no. I love women's singles," Se Young said.
When asked if she would try women's doubles, Se Young named compatriots Kim Ga Eun (world No. 13) and Sim Yu Jin (world No. 16) as potential partners.
"Oh yes, I want to try women's doubles. Ga Eun plays very well, and Yu Jin is also a very good doubles player. The two are really good players in women's doubles," she said.
A post shared by Badminton World Federation (@bwf.official)
Se Young, who won gold at the 2024 Paris Olympics, has claimed nine of the 11 tournaments she has played this year.
While women's singles remains her main focus, she said she would be open to a doubles appearance in the future.
79b32d5aa1f1285c: KUALA LUMPUR: Residents in Bukit Jalil, Bandar Kinrara, and Taman Puncak Jalil have urged Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim to review the proposed 17,000-unit Bandar Madani development in Bukit Jalil, citing severe traffic congestion and strained public amenities.
Protest committee chairman Zainuddin Zainal said the objection was not aimed at blocking development, but to ensure the high-density proposal was reassessed against current local conditions.

"We are not against development in the area, but we object because this high-intensity development does not take into account the current situation, particularly traffic congestion and other issues," he said.
"We want an engagement session involving Kuala Lumpur City Hall (DBKL), the government, local residents, and members of parliament so that the problems we face in this area can be addressed."
Zainuddin was speaking to reporters after the Coalition of Residents' Associations Against the Construction of 17,000 Apartments in Bukit Jalil held a peaceful demonstration outside Parliament today.
The coalition submitted a memorandum signed by 75 organisations to Seputeh MP Teresa Kok to be handed to the prime minister.

Zainuddin added that the proposed development allegedly contravened plot ratio controls under the Kuala Lumpur Local Plan 2040 (PTKL2040), as the proposed ratio was significantly higher than permitted under the plan.
He noted that residents were informed that a review was being conducted on an application to amend PTKL2040 to reduce plot ratio controls at the project site.
"However, questions arise as the first phase of the project has already opened for registration while the review of the plan is allegedly still ongoing," he said.

He urged the government to take residents' concerns seriously and prioritise essential infrastructure, including schools, a government hospital, Light Rail Transit (LRT) or Mass Rapid Transit (MRT) stations, flood retention ponds, upgraded fire and police stations, and green spaces.

The planned 26-hectare development comprises 17,000 apartment units, with 10 per cent allocated for affordable housing. The project is expected to bring an influx of about 51,000 residents, potentially impacting an estimated 74,324 existing residential units housing 209,908 residents within a 3km radius.

Residents also raised concerns over a proposed vertical school containing 104 classrooms. According to PLANMalaysia urban planning guidelines, a development serving 51,000 residents requires a school capacity of 511 classrooms.

Meanwhile, Kok said she would forward the memorandum to the prime minister and urged the government to postpone apartment registrations until studies on PTKL2040 and the Bukit Jalil Micro Control Plan are completed.
She said the developer, a subsidiary under the Housing and Local Government Ministry, had failed to comply with urban planning guidelines regarding social amenities and school capacity.
Reports on Oct 9 stated that Bandar Madani Bukit Jalil would be developed as a residential area equipped with amenities, including a vertical school.
Anwar, when tabling Budget 2027, said registration for the first phase would open the following Monday.
93655f41223bf6a0: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 14 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim described the implementation of the Parliamentary Services Act 2025 as a key step by the MADANI Government towards fulfilling its reform pledge to the people, including limiting powers traditionally held by the government.

He said the move was a key pillar of the country’s reform agenda, reflecting the government’s commitment to strengthening Parliament’s independence and advancing the maturity of the country’s parliamentary democracy.
“I consider this change and the Parliamentary Services Act important because they give meaning to parliamentary democracy and reflect the maturity of our democratic system.

“This is one of the important steps that I regard as a cornerstone of the MADANI Government’s reform agenda – fulfilling our promise to the people by introducing and passing the Parliamentary Services Act to limit powers traditionally held by the government,” he said.

Anwar was speaking at the Malaysian Parliament’s Administrative Transition and Institutional Reform ceremony, held at the Parliament Building here today in conjunction with the implementation of the Parliamentary Services Act 2025. — Bernama
b09ef582eb305dbd: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 14 — What if some of pop culture’s most famous rivals settled their differences in the Street Fighter arena?

As fans gear up for the upcoming live-action Street Fighter film, pixel artist Jude Buffum has been drawing attention with artwork reimagining familiar characters in the style of the classic fighting game.
Shared on the official Street Fighter movie Instagram account, the pixel art places characters from different franchises in one-on-one face-offs inspired by the game’s iconic combat screens.
Among the match-ups are Snake Eyes and Storm Shadow from the G.I. Joe franchise, as well as Transformers arch-enemies Optimus Prime and Megatron.
The artwork also imagines a showdown between Leonardo and Raphael from Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles (TMNT), bringing the brothers’ rivalry into the Street Fighter universe.
Even SpongeBob SquarePants gets a fighting-game twist, with SpongeBob and his longtime nemesis Plankton going head-to-head in the familiar arcade-style format.

The crossovers offer a playful take on the rivalries that have kept audiences invested in these franchises, from bitter enemies and competing warriors to brothers who often find themselves on opposing sides.

Snake Eyes and Storm Shadow from G.I. Joe clash in a pixel art scene inspired by Street Fighter. — Picture via Instagram/streetfightermovie
Buffum’s artwork draws on the retro pixel aesthetic associated with classic arcade games, recreating the face-off format that precedes a fight in Street Fighter.
The illustrations have prompted fans to call for the match-ups to become actual games, with some expressing excitement over the unlikely combinations.
One commenter reacting to the G.I. Joe artwork wrote: “Don’t be teasing us with this awesome-looking game that we probably won’t get!”

The Transformers illustration also drew calls for a fighting game, with one commenter saying: “We need this as a fighting video game,” while another said it reminded them of a classic comic featuring the characters.
Meanwhile, the TMNT crossover prompted speculation about a possible collaboration, with one fan asking: “TMNT vs Street Fighter movie confirmed?”
The SpongeBob illustration proved equally appealing to fans, with one commenter writing: “This actually looks like one of those SpongeBob flash games and I absolutely want more of this now.”

Another reaction to the Instagram posts summed up the excitement with: “Marketing is going crazy.”
The individual posts have attracted between 1,000 and 11,000 likes, reflecting the interest generated by the crossovers.
The artwork arrives ahead of the new film’s theatrical release on October 15 in Malaysia and October 16 in other markets.
The upcoming adaptation stars Andrew Koji as Ryu, Noah Centineo as Ken Masters, and Callina Liang as Chun-Li, alongside Jason Momoa as Blanka and Curtis “50 Cent” Jackson as Balrog.
The storyline is set in 1993, where estranged fighters Ryu and Ken Masters are recruited by Chun-Li to enter the next World Warrior Tournament.
Unbeknownst to them, this tournament will force the two fighters to face each other and their demons.
The film brings Capcom’s long-running fighting game series to the big screen once again, introducing its characters and martial arts rivalries to audiences beyond the gaming community.
b6f4b06f5ee9551a: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 14 — The Malaysian Pharmacists Society (MPS) has welcomed the government’s move to recommend contract pharmacy officers for permanent posts, but insists Putrajaya must quickly settle the critical details on quota figures, eligibility rules, and an implementation timeline.

The response follows remarks by Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad, who confirmed on Monday that the Ministry of Health (MOH) will submit a proposal to the Ministry of Finance and the Cabinet to absorb contract pharmacy officers into permanent positions.
He said permanent posts for dental and pharmacy personnel will come from a distinct allocation, separate from the 9,000 permanent medical officer positions unveiled under Budget 2027.

In a statement today, MPS singled out this dedicated quota and the pledge of a reasonable timeframe as encouraging signals for thousands of young officers who continue to staff public hospitals and clinics amid persistent career uncertainty.
Figures from the society show that 3,545 contract pharmacists remained on MOH rosters as of July 2026, while another 115 sat on the reserve list or awaited formal appointment.
“The latest clarification provides an important indication of the Government’s policy direction,” MPS president Prof Ph. Amrahi Buang said in the statement.
“The priority now is to translate this commitment into a clear, transparent and implementable pathway.”

To turn this commitment into reality, the society is seeking urgent clarification on the exact number of permanent positions to be created and when the proposal will reach the Cabinet and the Treasury.

It also wants transparent criteria detailing which cohorts will qualify, whether the 115 candidates on reserve will receive priority placement, and what options remain for those who have already exhausted their contract tenure but still wish to serve in the public healthcare system.

The society also urged authorities to reveal how evaluation panels will weigh clinical experience, seniority, and local staffing needs during the selection process, including whether appointments will be phased.

While MPS acknowledged that opening permanent posts demands seamless coordination between MOH, the Public Services Department, and the Treasury, it warned that prolonged ambiguity risks driving talent out of the public sector.

Beyond immediate absorption, the society also called on Putrajaya to weave these measures into a long-term pharmacy workforce strategy that reflects evolving clinical roles, frontline workload, and talent retention.
MPS pledged to work closely with MOH and central agencies through its Public Pharmacists Chapter, urging regular public updates as the Cabinet paper takes shape.
Contract dentistry faces a parallel challenge. The Malaysian Dental Association recently pressed Putrajaya for equitable treatment following the medical officer intake.
Addressing dental officers whose contracts ended without renewal, Dzulkefly maintained that MOH will keep monitoring their welfare and recognise their public service record.

During the same broadcast, Dzulkefly also expressed hope that the Treasury would clear a RM100 million seed grant to scale up non-communicable disease interventions across primary healthcare clinics nationwide.
85d7afb59de72935: KUALA LUMPUR: Foreign-linked companies operating in Malaysia contributed 17.1 per cent to the national economy in 2024, according to the Statistics Department.

In its Statistics on Foreign Affiliates in Malaysia 2024 report, the department said the value added by these companies rose 1.44 per cent to RM323.1 billion in 2024 from RM318.5 billion a year earlier.
Compared with 2020 when economic activity was affected by the Covid-19 pandemic, the value added grew by 34.1 per cent from RM241 billion.
The number of foreign-linked companies operating in Malaysia climbed four per cent to 3,230 in 2024 from 3,101 in 2023, while their workforce grew to 983,512 employees from 945,436.
Total employee compensation also rose 3.6 per cent to RM60 billion from RM57.9 billion, the department said.
The manufacturing sector remained the largest contributor to foreign-linked companies' value add, rising 4.7 per cent to RM165.4 billion in 2024 from RM158 billion in 2023.
The services sector followed, with the value add increasing 6.4 per cent to RM83.1 billion from RM78.1 billion.
However, value add in mining and quarrying slipped 0.89 per cent to RM77.8 billion from RM78.5 billion, the department stated.
Construction jumped 18 per cent to RM4 billion from RM3.4 billion, while agriculture remained unchanged at RM600 million.
By region, Asia accounted for the largest number of foreign-linked companies operating in Malaysia, with 2,074, or 64.2 per cent of the total.
Europe followed with 673 companies, representing 20.8 per cent, while the Americas accounted for 412, or 12.8 per cent.
MALAYSIAN FIRMS ABROAD'S TURNOVER ROSE
Meanwhile, turnover generated by Malaysian companies operating overseas rose 8.3 per cent to RM371.9 billion in 2024 from RM343.3 billion in 2023.
The Statistics on Malaysian Affiliates Abroad 2024 report showed that the number of Malaysian companies operating overseas edged up to 2,413 in 2024 from 2,404 a year earlier.
Their total workforce declined to 433,801 employees from 437,484, while employee compensation grew 6.3 per cent to RM27.1 billion from RM25.5 billion.

The services sector accounted for the largest share of overseas turnover, contributing RM252.1 billion, or 68 per cent of the total, up nearly 10 per cent from RM229.6 billion, or 66.9 per cent, in 2023.
Manufacturing turnover rose two per cent to RM63.2 billion from RM61.9 billion, although its share of total turnover declined to 17 per cent from 18 per cent.
Agriculture recorded stronger growth, with turnover jumping 25 per cent to RM20.3 billion from RM16.2 billion. Its share of total turnover rose to 5.5 per cent from 4.7 per cent.
Indonesia was the largest contributor among the major overseas markets, generating RM68.9 billion in turnover, or 18.5 per cent of the total, up 75 per cent from RM39.4 billion in 2023.
Turnover generated in Vietnam rose sharply to RM38.1 billion from RM3.9 billion, while the United Kingdom recorded an increase to RM27.3 billion from RM6.2 billion.
In contrast, turnover from Singapore dipped 48 per cent to RM29.1 billion from RM55.8 billion, while Australia's contribution fell 59 per cent to RM22.3 billion from RM54.7 billion.

4fba16b0036ba8e4: BANGKOK, Oct 14 — International Monetary Fund head Kristalina Georgieva said today that recent attacks on Saudi Arabia could impact people “everywhere”, as conflict in the energy-rich region adds to wide-ranging economic concerns.
A violent battle between a Saudi-led coalition and Yemen’s Houthis has erupted in recent days, with missile strikes on airports and energy facilities across the kingdom.
The latest round of fighting was triggered by Houthi strikes on Riyadh’s international airport at the weekend that left 13 people dead and operations suspended in the worst attack since 2015.

The escalation compounds fears about the impact of the Middle East crisis on global growth, with crude prices sent soaring since Iran effectively shut the crucial Strait of Hormuz after it was attacked by the US and Israel in February.
“The Saudi economy is important for the region and the world,” IMF managing director Georgieva said at a news conference during the Annual Meetings of the Fund and World Bank in Bangkok.
“In that sense, these developments have potentially negative spillovers for everybody, everywhere,” she said.

The warning comes as officials and experts gather in the Thai capital to discuss challenges facing the global economy, including higher energy costs and concerns about the sustainability of an artificial intelligence boom.
Other hurdles include ballooning debt in advanced economies, with bond yields at multi-decade highs as pressure grows on central banks to hike interest rates to cool inflation.
“What is our loudest call to policymakers right now? Make urgent repairs to the fiscal house before the cracks widen,” Georgieva said.
“Now is the time to enhance revenues, to rationalise spending and improve public financial management.”
‘Reaching limits’
In its closely watched World Economic Outlook released yesterday, the IMF raised its 2026 global growth forecast by 0.1 percentage points to 3.1 per cent.
However, it warned that while new economic activity has been sparked by rising investment in AI, poorer countries are not benefiting as they deal with soaring energy costs.
The global economy “remains resilient in the face of very frequent repetitive shocks and in the face of uncertainty”, Georgieva said. “But this resilience is reaching its limits.”
The IMF chief called for greater support for low-income countries to “strengthen their fundamentals so they can withstand shocks”.
She noted that a global rise in interest rates had also caused debt servicing costs to increase from around six per cent of government revenues a decade ago to 14 per cent today.
And in its Global Policy Agenda released today, the Fund warned that debt servicing challenges had become particularly acute for “low-income and vulnerable economies”.
Georgieva said the IMF had been “ringing the alarm bell on excessive global economic imbalances growing”.
“To put it very simply, China needs to spend more, the US has to save more and Europe has to invest more,” she added.

Advanced economies have seen their debt-to-GDP ratios skyrocket since the Covid-19 pandemic and wars in Ukraine and the Middle East, with governments forced to increase spending to cushion the impact of those shocks.
In China, a persistent slump in domestic demand has coincided with a historic surge in exports, accumulating trade surpluses that are becoming more and more politically problematic abroad.
Addressing the issue of how to tackle spiking bond yields, Georgieva admitted “there is no magic”.
“You have to go in a direction of tightening debt (and) bringing it down,” she said.
“(The) message that we are sending to our members: fundamentals matter. Get your house in order; otherwise, your people, your businesses will pay a price.” — AFP

31ca43969db2c7f8: KUALA LUMPUR: The government aims to create 500,000 job opportunities through artificial intelligence (AI)-related plans, in line with efforts to upgrade workforce skills to meet changes in the labour market.

Economy Minister Akmal Nasrullah Mohd Nasir told the Dewan Rakyat today that developments in AI, digitalisation and automation should be viewed as opportunities to restructure the economy, particularly by expanding high-growth, high-value (HGHV) industries and other high-impact strategic sectors.

"The challenge is how to increase the adoption of technology to facilitate work or improve workforce efficiency," he said in reply to a supplementary question from Datuk Awang Hashim (PN-Pendang) on the number of workers affected by AI technology and efforts to upgrade skills to address the challenge.

He said last year, 57 per cent of the workforce were in semi-skilled jobs with another 12.9 per cent were in low-skilled occupations, while a Stanford University study published last month stated that generative AI benefited experienced and highly skilled workers but posed challenges for those in low-skilled jobs.
"Under the 13th Malaysia Plan (13MP), the government aims to increase the proportion of skilled jobs to 35 per cent of the workforce by 2030, from 30.1 per cent in 2025," he said.

Replying to the original question from Jimmy Puah Wee Tse (PH-Tebrau) on measures to provide a clear workforce transition plan in response to AI, automation and digitalisation, Akmal said national policies and development plans also took into account talent requirements to address technological changes.
These included the 13MP, the New Industrial Master Plan 2030 (NIMP 2030), the National Energy Transition Roadmap (NETR), the National Semiconductor Strategy and the Malaysia Digital Action Plan 2030.

Meanwhile, he said a study by Talent Corporation Malaysia Bhd in November 2024 had found that 90 per cent of existing jobs would remain relevant through skills adaptation, while 10 per cent faced the impact of automation or job functions changes due to AI developments, digitalisation and the green economy.

"To ensure that developments in AI, digitalisation and automation do not lead to large-scale job losses, talent development programmes covering certification, upskilling and reskilling will continue to be strengthened.

"Cooperation between the public sector, industry and academia will be intensified for this purpose, including through the MyMahir Future Skills Talent Council (MyMahir FSTC). A total of 17 MyMahir FSTCs have been established, each chaired by a different industry player," he said.
3a6f4cb08130a674: KUALA LUMPUR: Bekas menteri luar, Saifuddin Abdullah (PN-Indera Mahkota), menggesa Perdana Menteri Anwar Ibrahim supaya tidak melantik seorang ulama Mesir ke dalam Majlis Penasihat Pondok dan Turath yang dicadangkan kerajaan.

Saifuddin merujuk rampasan kuasa di Mesir pada 2013, apabila menteri pertahanan ketika itu, Abdel Fattah el-Sisi, menggulingkan Presiden Mohamed Morsi.
Menurut Human Rights Watch, pasukan keselamatan membunuh sekurang-kurangnya 817 penunjuk perasaan semasa tindakan keras di Dataran Rabaa, Kaherah.

“Ramai lagi ulama tempatan, di Indonesia dan Timur Tengah yang boleh kita rujuk untuk mendapatkan nasihat yang baik.”

3a0cd53682d224ba: AYUTTHAYA, Oct 14 — Stilt houses in villages north of Bangkok are no longer high enough to stay dry as Thai authorities deliberately flood riverside communities to spare the capital.

Inside the home of Kamonchanok Sathaphonamonwut, raised more than three metres (10 feet) above the ground in Ayutthaya province, her family of three sleeps on makeshift platforms and cannot use the waterlogged toilet.
Her village has been flooded six years in a row, pushing some to move away, while others have raised their houses higher.
“Our area simply cannot cope with this much water anymore,” the 34-year-old told AFP, wading through her soaked home.
But while authorities prioritise protecting Bangkok and other business hubs from floods, “when it comes to our residential communities, they neglect us”, she said.
Thailand experiences flooding every year during the monsoon season, and scientists say human-made climate change has made heavy rain and floods more frequent and severe.

After devastating floods in 2011, the government expanded embankments, water gates and other infrastructure to direct water away from Bangkok, the historic city of Ayutthaya and industrial zones along the Chao Phraya River, which flows through the capital.
The defences have largely kept commercial centres safe, but residents of other areas have been left to fend for themselves.

Around 20 kilometres (12 miles) from Ayutthaya’s centuries-old temple ruins, a Unesco heritage site, residents say floods that once reached their knees now rise above their heads in some areas and can take several months to recede.
Office worker Kamonchanok has been forced to commute by boat, and hoist her household appliances and other belongings above the waterline.
“All we can do is deal with the consequences,” she said.
“There’s only so much we can do to adapt.”
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
A father removes a flotation vest worn by his daughter in front of their flooded home in Bang Ban district in the central Thai province of Ayutthaya on October 7, 2026. — AFP pic
‘Cruel’ but effective

Thai irrigation department spokesman Thanet Somboon said climate change, low-lying geography and recently built embankments that altered the natural flow of the Chao Phraya have contributed to more severe flooding of downstream communities.
“Even when water is released from the Chao Phraya Dam at the same rate as before, the impact is greater than it used to be,” Thanet told AFP.
And after irrigation channels were completely full of diverted water, he said authorities had “no choice but to discharge the remaining water downstream”.
But Thanet acknowledged that officials may need to review infrastructure to “ensure floodwater can be kept within the intended limits”.
Environmental conservationist Sasin Chalermlarp said the government has done “an excellent job” managing floods across the central plains.
But its efforts were “cruel” to those bearing the brunt of the flooding.

In low-lying riverside districts that serve as flood retention zones, AFP journalists saw stretches of villages underwater this month, with some homes abandoned and others submerged up to their roofs.
Sasin said floodwater that once spread across much of Ayutthaya is now concentrated in just “five to 10 per cent” of the province.
Rising costs
As flooding in hard-hit districts has become more severe, many who remain have paid to lift their stilt houses higher and keep their living space dry.
Kamonchanok’s family raised their home twice in the 1990s, the second time by 1.5 metres.
But floodwater reached their house in 2011, and again for the past six consecutive years.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->

Thai retiree Somjit Kitklin, 93 (centre), sits on a raised metal‑and‑wood platform as her son Sommai Kitklin, 63, stands in floodwater inside their home in Sena district, Ayutthaya province, October 7, 2026. — AFP pic
Raising a house can cost between 100,000 and one million baht (RM12,166-RM121,663), depending on its size and height, residents say.
Some families have lifted their homes twice in just a few years, exhausting their savings and borrowing to get by.
Despite spending more than one million baht raising her home, Sawong Raksri, 87, is unfazed.
“It floods like this every year recently. What’s the point of complaining?” she said.
‘Flood-free tax’
Sasin acknowledged that the area’s low-lying land made it a natural route for floodwater.
“But the villagers have no choice. They are being forced to make sacrifices,” he said.
Sasin, who lives in a protected part of Ayutthaya, has proposed a “flood-free tax” on those who benefit from the defences, to help impacted families raise their homes and repair damage.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
A vendor sells prepared food from her boat as she paddles past a flooded shrine in Sena district in the central Thai province of Ayutthaya on October 7.
Thanet from the irrigation department said the idea warranted further study to determine “how to support people who sacrifice their land to accommodate floodwater”.

The government’s flagship fix is a US$780-million flood diversion canal, designed to carry 1,200 cubic metres of water — around half the volume of an Olympic-size swimming pool — per second around the bottleneck where the Chao Phraya narrows through Ayutthaya.
It is expected to be completed by 2030.

Until then, Kamonchanok said her community was not even demanding an end to intentional flooding, but rather a cap on water levels and financial support for those whose homes sit below the flood line.
“All we’re asking for is to be able to live comfortably in our own homes,” she said.
“Why can’t they give us that?” — AFP

deb3f38d5bc679e4: KOTA KINABALU, Oct 14 — Sabah’s economy grew by 5.1 per cent last year, its strongest performance in six years, with gross domestic product (GDP) reaching RM88.8 billion, said Chief Minister Datuk Seri Hajiji Noor.
He said the growth was supported by the services sector, which expanded by 4.5 per cent, manufacturing (five per cent) and construction (28.3 per cent).

He expressed hope that the collaboration would evolve into a broader strategic partnership delivering lasting economic benefits to Sabah.
8da9e41c68aa6272: TAIPEI: Taiwan said Wednesday it will inject up to US$4.4 billion in the Alaska LNG project, after US President Donald Trump announced the island's investment in the to-be-built natural gas pipeline.
Taiwan imports nearly all of its energy supply and has sought to shore up Washington's support as China presses its claims of sovereignty over the island democracy.
"According to current plans, the cooperation will include the annual procurement of six million metric tons of Alaska LNG following production," the Ministry of Economic Affairs said in a statement.
It will also involve "participation in project development, with an estimated investment of up to US$4.4 billion," the ministry said.
"If the project progresses smoothly according to the planned timeline, it is expected to begin further supplementing domestic natural gas supplies as early as 2032," it added.

The statement came hours after Trump told a rally in Wasilla, Alaska, that Taiwan had agreed to buy 30 percent of the output from the pipeline over the next 20 year and also invest US$4.4 billion into the project.
Taiwan sources its LNG from multiple countries but the mix has changed dramatically this year after the start of the Middle East war when Iran claimed control of the Strait of Hormuz.
Australia replaced Qatar as Taiwan's biggest supplier of LNG, accounting for 34.8 percent of imports, Taiwanese official data for the first eight months of 2026 show.
Qatari LNG made up 10.7 percent, compared with 35.1 percent in the same period last year, while imports from the United States more than tripled to account for 24.5 percent.
Taiwan's government has previously acknowledged the island's intent to buy LNG from Alaska.
- 'Stability and resilience' -

The Ministry of Economic Affairs said in early 2025 that Taiwan's state-owned energy company CPC Corporation "will procure LNG and seek upstream investment participation rights to secure a stable future energy supply for Taiwan".
"The government's role is to ensure the stability and resilience of the entire energy supply -- I believe this is true for governments around the world," Premier Cho Jung-tai said Wednesday.

"We, of course, are on a very long journey in this regard, and we have been working tirelessly to maintain a stable domestic supply of oil, electricity, and natural gas -- as we have done from the beginning of this year until now."
Trump said the deal "guarantees" the success of the project.

7ca15df3c3914e23: PUTRAJAYA: Malaysians in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, are safe and have not been affected by Houthi attacks in the country so far, says Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan.

He said the ministry received daily reports from the Malaysian Embassy in Riyadh and the Malaysian Consulate in Jeddah to monitor the safety and welfare of Malaysians working and studying in Saudi Arabia.
However, Malaysians there have been advised to avoid public areas and strategic locations that could be potential targets. They have also been told to remain at home unless it is necessary to go out.
They are also encouraged to use the e-Konsular facility to contact the embassy if they need assistance.
"The Malaysian Embassy remains in contact with Malaysians in the country to ensure their welfare and safety," he said at a press conference today.
Media reports said about 250 Malaysian students studying in Riyadh, Madinah and Makkah were safe, with lectures continuing as usual.

Following an attack at King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, several universities in the city reportedly began conducting classes online from last Sunday. In Makkah and Madinah, classes continued in person.
Mohamad said some Malaysians were temporarily stranded in Jeddah following the cancellation of return flights, as several airlines, including Malaysian carriers, were unable to operate.
However, the situation was temporary, with Malaysia Airlines offering affected passengers accommodation at locations designated by the airline and making alternative flight arrangements.
Mohamad said Malaysians without urgent reasons to travel to Saudi Arabia had been advised to reschedule their trips as the security situation remained unsettled.
5369002d1f5008dc: WASHINGTON: US President Donald Trump said on Wednesday that plans were underway for major oil, gas and mineral exploration in Greenland, claiming the Arctic island holds vast, easily accessible oil resources amid months of elevated global energy prices, Anadolu Ajansi (AA) reported.

"Massive Oil, Gas, and Mineral Exploration is getting ready to begin in our new and beautiful Greenland!" Trump wrote on his social media platform Truth Social, as global energy prices remain elevated more than seven months into the war in Iran.
He suggested that some experts believe Greenland has some of the world's largest easily accessible oil reserves, though he provided no details about the estimates or planned exploration activities.
Trump also emphasised Greenland's strategic location, arguing it would play a central role in defending the US and Europe against future attacks.
"Any future attack on the United States will have to come across Greenland, where our Defence will routinely knock down drones, missiles, or any other form of weapon not yet even conceived," he said.

Greenland stopped issuing new oil and gas exploration licences in 2021 over environmental and climate concerns, although previously granted licences remain valid.
dae634cdb032e6f1: BANGKOK: International Monetary Fund head Kristalina Georgieva said Wednesday that recent attacks on Saudi Arabia could impact people "everywhere", as conflict in the energy-rich region adds to wide-ranging economic concerns.

e64144e758caabe0: LONDON: Al-Hilal secured a 2-0 win over Qatar's Al-Sadd in Doha on Tuesday with Ollie Watkins' improvised finish sending the Saudi Pro League outfit on their way to a second successive Asian Champions League Elite win.
The former Aston Villa striker netted in the 40th minute to give Al-Hilal the lead, calmly steering the ball home while lying on the turf after being upended in the penalty area by Agustin Soria.

The win followed Al-Hilal's opening victory over Al-Gharafa in the western league phase of the competition last month and was sealed when Ruben Neves scored from the penalty spot in the 65th minute.
Al-Hilal were joined on six points by Shabab Al-Ahli after the side from the United Arab Emirates beat former champions Al-Ittihad 2-1 in Jeddah.

7033ba9df13b0ac6: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 14 — KnowBe4, a digital workforce security company, has found that more than a third (36 per cent) of Singapore office workers are not confident they could distinguish a genuine message from their chief executive officer (CEO) from one generated using artificial intelligence (AI), including voice cloning and deepfake technology.

The findings are from a report titled “Would You Know Your CEO’s Real Voice? Singapore’s Growing Deepfake Vulnerability”, based on a Censuswide survey of 500 office workers in Singapore. KnowBe4 released the report during Singapore International Cyber Week and GovWare.
In a statement, KnowBe4 Chief Information Security Officer advisor, Dr Kawin Boonyapredee said Singapore hierarchy works like a trust shortcut, one that AI-enabled scams are now designed to exploit.

“A cloned voice or a convincing message from ‘the boss’ doesn’t need to fool the technology. It only needs to activate an instinct not to question authority,” he said, adding that organisations need training and simulations to change behaviour at every level of seniority.

The research highlights a dual vulnerability in Singapore workplaces, where junior and middle-tier employees may hesitate to question senior leaders, while senior managers can be overconfident in their ability to identify deepfakes.

Half of the respondents (50 per cent) said they would feel uncomfortable challenging a request from a senior executive, while 52 per cent were concerned about potential negative consequences for doing so.

Meanwhile, 45 per cent said they would be equally worried about delaying a senior leader’s request as about accidentally causing a cybersecurity incident, while nine per cent would rather risk a security breach than delay their boss’s request.

Senior managers were the most confident in their ability to identify a fake, with 78 per cent expressing confidence. However, they were also the most likely to comply with a cloned CEO voice before verifying it, at 35 per cent, more than double the 16 per cent recorded among clerical workers.

Only 26 per cent of respondents had received training specifically addressing AI-generated scams involving senior leaders. Just 10 per cent identified employees trusting senior leaders too readily as the greatest cybersecurity risk in their workplace, suggesting that the vulnerability may be under-recognised.

The report said technology alone would not be sufficient to address increasingly convincing AI-enabled impersonation targeting senior leaders. Organisations also need to foster an environment in which junior and middle-tier employees feel safe speaking up, while encouraging senior managers to adopt stronger verification practices rather than relying on confidence alone. — Bernama
cb0a83b23dc1b69d: GEORGE TOWN: A government agency chairman with the title Datuk is expected to be charged at the Special Corruption Sessions Court tomorrow.
The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) has obtained approval to charge the chairman under Op Jurus, with proceedings set for 9am.
Lawyer Dr Shamsher Singh Thind, who represents the chairman, confirmed that his client would be charged.
"Yes, he will be charged alone. That was what I was told," he said when contacted.
However, the nature of the charge is not yet known.
On Aug 26, the 53-year-old chairman was released on RM10,000 bail after completing a week-long remand extension granted by the magistrates' court.
His brother, sister-in-law and two company directors were also remanded in connection with the case.

The investigation centres on allegations that the chairman abused his position as deputy chairman and board member to approve the sale of eight plots of land in Seberang Perai Selatan to a company allegedly owned by an associate in 2015.
The sale was below market value, resulting in estimated losses of RM1.96 million.
9159413f051c414f: KUALA LUMPUR: Investors in Malaysia should be assessed on the quality of jobs they create and how they treat workers, particularly women, said Malaysian Investment Development Authority (MIDA) chairman Tengku Datuk Seri Zafrul Abdul Aziz.
He said fair wages, safe workplaces and flexible working arrangements should be key criteria for quality investments.
"The investors we welcome to Malaysia should be judged by how they treat the women who work for them. Good jobs, fair pay, safe workplaces and flexible work.
"These are not favours. They are the new standard of a quality investment," he said in his keynote address at the Annual Women Economic Forum and G100 Global Meet 2026 here today.

Citing McKinsey research, Tengku Zafrul said advancing women's equality could add US$4.5 trillion annually to Asia-Pacific economies, with Malaysia potentially gaining about US$50 billion a year, equivalent to roughly eight per cent of its gross domestic product.
He said greater workforce participation by women, alongside equal access to capital and markets for women entrepreneurs, would expand the economy's productive capacity.

"When more women enter and remain in the workforce, women entrepreneurs have equal access to capital and markets, and talented women can rise into senior leadership, we expand the productive capacity of the entire economy.
"We enlarge the pool of ideas, skills and enterprise from which growth is created," he said.

He noted that Malaysia's female labour force participation rate reached a record 56.6 per cent at the end of 2025, but many women left the workforce after graduation because of inadequate childcare support and caregiving responsibilities.
He said women often had to balance their careers with caring for children and ageing parents, highlighting the need to address these barriers to enable more women to remain economically active.
Tengku Zafrul said empowering women was essential to unlocking Malaysia's economic potential, particularly as countries competed for talent, productivity and innovation.
"In a world where every country is competing for talent, productivity and innovation, leaving women behind is not simply unjust, it is economically irrational," he said.
0b3a62f01969ac5f: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 14 —A former e-hailing driver was sentenced to eight years and six months’ imprisonment by the High Court in Johor Bahru today for abusing a three-year-old boy in 2022, which included forcing the child to eat his own excrement.
Chan Wen Jie, 32, pleaded guilty before Judicial Commissioner Datuk Abdul Fareed Abdul Gafoor to an alternative charge of child abuse under Section 31(1)(a) of the Child Act 2001, FMT reported.
The father of two was ordered to serve his sentence from his arrest on Oct 3, 2022, perform 36 hours of community service within six months, and execute a three-year good behaviour bond.
In his judgment, Fareed rejected the defence’s argument that the acts, captured on closed-circuit television, were merely intended to discipline the toddler.
“The accused not only caned the victim but also slapped him, hit him on the head and forced him to do squats, stand for long periods and eat his faeces from his disposable diaper.

“Forcing the child to eat faeces was a cruel and degrading act that could in no way be considered a form of discipline. If the accused was unable to care for the victim, he should have handed the child back to his father,” he said.
Chan was originally charged in 2022 with murdering the boy, Lee See Jie, at a house in Taman Skudai Ria, Skudai, on Oct 2.

The capital murder charge was subsequently withdrawn, with the court clarifying that it did not weigh the initial murder charge or the child’s cause of death when determining the sentence for the abuse offence.
Deputy Public Prosecutors Edelynn Wong and Nur Diyana Zubir prosecuted, while K. Sarawanakumar and Freda Sabapathy represented Chan.
242de8c988af6071: JOHOR BARU: A former e-hailing driver was sentenced to eight years and six months in jail for abusing a three-year-old boy and forcing him to eat his own faeces in 2022.
Judicial Commissioner Datuk Abdul Fareed Abdul Gapoor sentenced Chan Wen Jie, 32, after he pleaded guilty to an alternative charge of abusing the child under Section 31(1) of the Child Act 2001.
The High Court ordered Chan to serve his sentence from the date of his arrest on Oct 3, 2022.
He was also ordered to enter into a three-year good behaviour bond with one surety without security and complete 36 hours of community service within six months.
In his grounds of judgment, Abdul Fareed described the act of forcing the boy to eat faeces from his disposable diaper as uncivilised, degrading and wholly unacceptable as a form of discipline.

The court also considered closed-circuit television (CCTV) footage showing Chan subjecting the boy to various forms of abuse, including banging his head, making him perform squats, forcing him to stand for prolonged periods and whipping him.

"The footage showed that the accused's actions went beyond ordinary physical punishment and amounted to excessive and merciless abuse of a three-year-old child who was unable to protect himself," the judge said.
Abdul Fareed said Chan had betrayed the trust placed in him by the boy's father, who had entrusted him with the child's care.
The judge said Chan should have returned the boy to his father if he was unable to care for him.
He also rejected the defence's argument that Chan had disciplined the boy in the same way he disciplined his own child.
However, the court did not consider the withdrawn murder charge under Section 302 of the Penal Code or the cause of the boy's death when determining the sentence for the child abuse offence.
After weighing the aggravating and mitigating factors, the court ruled that the sentence was appropriate for the offence and stressed the need to protect children from abuse.
On Oct 13, 2022, Chan was charged with murdering Lee See Jie, 3, at a house in Jalan Ria 2, Taman Skudai Ria, Skudai, between 8pm and 8.30pm on Oct 2, 2022.
Deputy public prosecutors Edelynn Wong and Nordiana Zubir prosecuted the case, while Chan was represented by lawyer K. Sarawanakumar.

19aa164eb576337c: KUALA LUMPUR: Former foreign minister Saifuddin Abdullah (PN-Indera Mahkota) today urged Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim not to appoint an Egyptian scholar to the government's new Islamic scholarship advisory council.

Saifuddin told the Dewan Rakyat that the cleric supported an army general who overthrew a democratically elected president in a Middle Eastern country, and justified the killing of thousands of the ousted leader’s supporters.

He did not name the scholar but was believed to be referring to Egypt’s former grand mufti Sheikh Ali Gomaa, whom Anwar had said would be involved in the "Malaysian pondok and turath advisory council".
"Do not appoint that wicked and cruel scholar. It would send the wrong message if we are serious about improving Islamic education for our children," Saifuddin said in debating the 2027 budget.

Saifuddin was referring to the 2013 coup in Egypt, when then defence minister Abdel Fattah el-Sisi ousted president Mohamed Morsi. Security forces killed at least 817 protesters during a crackdown in Cairo’s Rabaa Square, according to Human Rights Watch.

Gomaa publicly supported the military and defended the use of deadly force against armed opponents. However, he denied issuing a religious ruling permitting the killing of peaceful protesters, saying his remarks concerned those who attacked security forces with weapons.
Anwar announced the advisory council in his budget speech last Friday, saying it was aimed at preserving traditional Islamic scholarship, or turath.
He named Gomaa and Morocco's Sheikh Idris al-Fasi as international scholars involved in the initiative, but did not specify their roles.
Saifuddin said Malaysia could appoint other Islamic scholars to the council instead. "There are many other scholars in Malaysia, Indonesia and the Middle East whom we can turn to for sound advice."
e40ddf593a297f51: HO CHI MINH CITY, Oct 14 — Vietnam held funeral rites for more than 700 of its war dead today, unearthed in a major push to identify those missing from decades of conflict with France and the United States.

Tens of thousands of people lined the streets of Ho Chi Minh City, some holding white flowers or praying as buses carrying terracotta caskets covered by Vietnam’s national flag moved in procession to a cemetery for fallen soldiers on the outskirts of the city.

The 731 sets of remains, taken from individual and mass graves of fighters killed when US-backed forces crushed an uprising by communists in 1968, were exhumed from a tree-shaded public park, according to the military.
Le Ngoc Mai Uyen was a frequent visitor to the park named after her grandmother, revolutionary fighter Le Thi Rieng, before she realised her relative’s body may be buried there.
“I have always felt something sacred here at this park,” the 36-year-old told AFP recently, after burning incense near a memorial plaque.
While she knew it was “extremely difficult”, Uyen said she has “strong faith” that the remains of her grandmother will be found.
The park was excavated as part of a 500-day national drive launched in March, touted as Vietnam’s largest push to locate some of the hundreds of thousands missing since the war.
Since July, hundreds of experts and soldiers have been working to unearth layers of remains at the park, aided by bulldozers, excavators and water pumps but often sifting through the mud by hand.

At the funeral service today, patriotic songs blaring, the city’s deputy mayor Nguyen Manh Cuong said authorities “will not overlook any opportunity or method to continue the journey of searching for the fallen comrades”.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
A casket bearing the remains of fallen soldier is seen at Le Thi Rieng Park in Ho Chi Minh City October 14, 2026. — AFP pic
Race against time
“Due to the ferocity of the war and the passage of so much time, we have not yet been able to identify the names or hometowns of most of the soldiers recovered in this phase,” Cuong said.
The government has announced the identity of one dead soldier, squad leader Huynh Van Quen who fought in 1968 and whose remains were found in Le Thi Rieng Park, according to state media.
Quen was identified in July thanks to a scrap of paper bearing his name that was found with his remains, and DNA samples that matched his relatives.
Up to 1.2 million Vietnamese soldiers are estimated to have been killed between 1945 and 1975, during wars involving former colonial power France, and then the United States as well as its allies.
There are 230,000 graves nationwide for unidentified soldiers, while thousands of others are believed to remain buried in remote jungles, or under farmland or other former battlefields.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->

Vietnam’s Prime Minister Le Minh Hung pays his respects with folded hands as he passes caskets bearing the remains of fallen soldiers at Le Thi Rieng Park in Ho Chi Minh City October 14, 2026. — AFP pic
The government aims to recover 7,000 sets of remains by July 2027, “a political task of special importance but also a command from the heart”, according to Deputy Prime Minister Pham Thi Thanh Tra.

More than 1,500 people have been deployed to search old battlefields in Vietnam, Laos and Cambodia — neighbouring countries drawn into the war — alongside thousands more engaged in data collection and analysis.
They are collecting samples from the 230,000 unidentified graves as well as conducting DNA analysis on 18,000 samples of remains and setting up a genetic database of their next of kin.
Colonel Trinh Tung Lam, part of the project’s command team, said their task was not easy, but it was the “right” time for this “most special and humane” effort.
In a lab at the Center for DNA Identification in Hanoi last week, technicians carefully cut into bone fragments separated from remains to extract samples for DNA analysis.
Director Tran Trung Thanh told AFP the state institution had acquired and developed “a world-first process for handling remains that have undergone severe degradation”.
Using US-funded technology through the International Commission on Missing Persons, a pilot programme had reported genetic data was successfully pulled from 54 of 58 samples, he said.
But he warned the process was “lengthy” — and they were in a race against time.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
People gather with flowers by a roadside as they wait for the vehicle transporting the remains of fallen soldiers to pass by in Ho Chi Minh City October 14, 2026. — AFP pic
‘Final hope’
“As the surviving relatives and close kin of the fallen age and pass away, we risk losing a vital source of reference data,” Thanh said.
Meanwhile, “the remains continue to decompose under natural conditions”, he said, making it harder to extract DNA.
For many, finding their loved ones has been a lifetime’s work.
Doan Van Cong, 68, and his family spent years touring cemeteries and talking to witnesses to discover what happened to his uncle, who died in 1950, when he was in his early 20s.
They believe he was among communist combatants buried in a mass grave 50 kilometres (30 miles) from his home after an ambush by French troops.
But “there were no opportunities to excavate” the suspected sites, he told AFP.
Now, Cong said, the government drive for answers is his “final hope”. — AFP
92a752bc5dc452f6: SEOUL: South Korea's football association has told fans to stop "excessive personal attacks", warning of the "psychological burden" it could inflict on national team players in the crosshairs since their World Cup flop.
Hong Myung-bo quit as coach after the team failed to advance past the group stage in North America, and Spanish interim Robert Moreno is awaiting word on a possible extension.
With the Asian Cup scheduled to take place in January in Saudi Arabia, the national side are engulfed by claims of internal divisions.
Local media reports say some younger players feel held back by senior members of the squad, including long-time captain Son Heung-min.
In a lengthy statement, the Korea Football Association condemned what it called attempts to sow discord.

"Unverified information and speculative claims about national football team players have recently been spreading on social media and online forums, with some players facing excessive criticism and personal attacks," the KFA said on Tuesday.

"Such behaviour goes beyond the bounds of legitimate criticism and can place a severe psychological burden on individual players," it said, urging fans to refrain from "making assumptions about internal team dynamics and fuelling divisions within the squad."

Speculation about discord emerged after Bayern Munich defender Kim Min-jae threw his boots in anger after being substituted in the second half of the disappointing home 0-0 draw with Venezuela this month.
Kim said afterwards that "every player needs to put their head down and give it their all", fuelling talk of divisions within the squad.
The latest firestorm follows public outrage over the behaviour of some players who earned exemptions from mandatory military service after winning gold at the Asian Games.

Their post-match celebrations, seen as suggesting that military exemptions had been their main motivation, sparked a backlash and prompted Defence Minister Kang Shin-chul to pledge to scale back the benefit.--AFP
7007091d2f607c92: LONDON: A London court was to hear opening arguments Wednesday on the first full day of British comedian and actor Russell Brand's trial for multiple charges of rape and sexual assault.

Once a left-wing personality and comedian who shot to fame as a television and radio presenter, Brand has reinvented himself as a conservative and faith-based guru for millions of social media followers.
The 51-year-old faces seven sexual offence charges involving six women, relating to a period between 1999 and 2009. The women's identities will not be revealed during the trial.
Brand has pleaded not guilty to all the charges – three counts of rape, three of sexual assault and one charge of indecent assault.
On Wednesday prosecutor Riel Karmy-Jones is expected to set out the allegations against Brand in full detail.
The trial at London's Southwark Crown Court should last around six weeks but could stretch into December.
This week, judge Joel Bennathan selected a jury, eliminating six who had seen a 2023 documentary about Brand or read a newspaper article making allegations about Brand.
The judge warned the jury, made up of eight men and four women, not to search online about Brand before reaching a verdict.
Brand cut a flamboyant figure at initial hearings, arriving Monday with his wife Laura Gallacher and a heavily tattooed security guard, sometimes wearing sunglasses and carrying a Bible.
There has been huge media interest in the case, and he told reporters Tuesday he felt "blessed."
During the trial he will sit in a glass-walled enclosure with his back to reporters, facing the judge.
The trial is attracting intense media scrutiny, with numerous British outlets launching dedicated podcasts and US channels reporting from outside the court.
Born to working-class parents in Essex in eastern England, Brand launched a successful stand-up comedy career as a teenager.
He became a household name as a television presenter on MTV, Channel Four and the BBC, also penning newspaper columns and two autobiographies.
- SEXUAL ASSAULTS -
He then made a foray into Hollywood, starring in several hit films, and was in a brief, but high-profile, marriage to US pop star Katy Perry.
Now remarried and living in Florida with his young family, he has gained a new following as an influencer, with six million subscribers on YouTube, 10.1 million on X and 4.9 million on Instagram.
After a police investigation, last year he was charged with two counts of rape, two of sexual assault and one of indecent assault dating between 1999 and 2005.
The term indecent assault is used for offences committed before 2004.
In February Brand pleaded not guilty to fresh charges of sexually assaulting a woman and raping another women in 2009.

At previous hearings it was said Brand is charged with raping a woman in a hotel room at the Labour Party conference in Bournemouth in 1999, grabbing a TV worker's breasts and forcing her into a sex act in a toilet, and kissing and groping a radio station worker.
The same London court held a high-profile trial of Oscar-winning actor Kevin Spacey, with a jury in 2023 finding him not guilty of nine alleged sex offences against four men.--AFP
