cdef0602b272d4e8: SAN FRANCISCO, Oct 14 — Small artificial intelligence models may be only months away from being able to behave like a computer worm, copying themselves from one internet-connected gadget to the next without human help, AI giant Anthropic said.
The finding potentially opens a new front in the cybersecurity threats emerging from AI, which have rattled governments and the companies rushing to adopt the technology.

The research, posted on an Anthropic blog late Monday, comes as tech companies race to build ever more powerful AI directly into phones, laptops, cars and household devices, rather than running it only in distant data centers.
A computer worm is malicious software that spreads between machines on its own. Researchers at Anthropic said an AI version would no longer need powerful data centers to operate.
Instead, it could hop from device to device across networks of cheap, poorly secured consumer hardware such as smart TV boxes and kitchen appliances.

The researchers based their calculations of how far such a worm could spread on Kimwolf, a botnet — a network of hijacked devices controlled by hackers — that infected more than two million devices at its peak, mostly off-brand Android TV boxes.

An AI worm of the kind described in the research would likely be slow, taking days to copy itself, William Zhou and Daniel Freeman of Anthropic said, comparing it to a slowly multiplying swarm of fruit flies.
Once created, it would be hard to stamp out, because there would be no central switch to turn off.
Anthropic’s researchers said their estimate of how fast and how far AI-fueled malware could spread was rough, since it was based on one type of gadget and one past botnet.

But over time, the amount of computing power sitting in everyday gadgets is expected to keep growing, while the AI models needed to pull this off are likely to keep getting smaller, the researchers added.

Varun Chandrasekaran, an assistant professor of electrical and computer engineering at the University of Illinois, said the research was unsurprising and matched similar recent findings, though he cautioned that Anthropic’s work had not been independently verified.
He also noted that security on devices like thermostats or home cameras “has historically been very weak.”
But when it came to AI, the biggest current threat was human bad actors using artificial intelligence to sharpen their hacks, rather than AI systems themselves going rogue, he said.
“A malicious human being is now supercharged with AI to perform bad things and we are seeing this happen at scale,” he added.

The rogue AI debate came to the fore in July, when AI programs running on OpenAI models escaped an internal company test and broke into the systems of AI platform Hugging Face—apparently hunting for the test’s answers.
The incident and subsequent reports like it have sparked international pressure for closer regulation of AI, even as the Trump administration resists the idea and urges the industry to police itself.

Anthropic and ChatGPT-maker OpenAI have been accused by powerful voices in the White House and Silicon Valley of stoking fears about AI and encouraging government rules in order to protect their market dominance from smaller rivals.

Brad Smith, OpenAI investor Microsoft’s president, warned Tuesday that industry and governments must “act with urgency” to create “real and effective safety standards” in order to rein in the risks of artificial intelligence. — AFP
a135f82a86136378: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 14 — Investors in Malaysia should be assessed on the quality of jobs they create and how they treat workers, particularly women, said Malaysian Investment Development Authority (Mida) chairman Tengku Datuk Seri Zafrul Abdul Aziz.
He said fair wages, safe workplaces and flexible working arrangements should be key criteria for quality investments.
“The investors we welcome to Malaysia should be judged by how they treat the women who work for them. Good jobs, fair pay, safe workplaces and flexible work.
“These are not favours. They are the new standard of a quality investment,” he said in his keynote address at the Annual Women Economic Forum and G100 Global Meet 2026 here today.

Citing McKinsey research, Tengku Zafrul said advancing women’s equality could add US$4.5 trillion (RM18.4 trillion) annually to Asia-Pacific economies, with Malaysia potentially gaining about US$50 billion a year, equivalent to roughly eight per cent of its gross domestic product.
He said greater workforce participation by women, alongside equal access to capital and markets for women entrepreneurs, would expand the economy’s productive capacity.

“When more women enter and remain in the workforce, women entrepreneurs have equal access to capital and markets, and talented women can rise into senior leadership, we expand the productive capacity of the entire economy.
“We enlarge the pool of ideas, skills and enterprise from which growth is created,” he said.

He noted that Malaysia’s female labour force participation rate reached a record 56.6 per cent at the end of 2025, but many women left the workforce after graduation because of inadequate childcare support and caregiving responsibilities.
He said women often had to balance their careers with caring for children and ageing parents, highlighting the need to address these barriers to enable more women to remain economically active.
Tengku Zafrul said empowering women was essential to unlocking Malaysia’s economic potential, particularly as countries competed for talent, productivity and innovation.
“In a world where every country is competing for talent, productivity and innovation, leaving women behind is not simply unjust, it is economically irrational,” he said. — Bernama
2fc5ccad0be59df4: WUHAN: Six-time Grand Slam champion Iga Swiatek launched her Wuhan Open campaign by triumphing 6-2, 6-1 in an all-Polish battle against lucky loser Magdalena Frech on Wednesday.
Swiatek posted her 40th victory of the season in one hour and 42 minutes and remains on course for a potential quarter-final showdown with top seed and three-time Wuhan winner Aryna Sabalenka.
"We know each other pretty well, so I just wanted to focus on being consistent and playing as good as possible," Swiatek, the seventh seed, said of Frech.

"I know she is running to every ball always and sometimes using the power of the opponent, so I wanted to not play too crazy but play solid and I’m happy that I did that," said Swiatek, who is chasing a qualification spot for the year-end WTA Finals.

Despite the lopsided scoreline the opening set was tight, lasting over an hour and requiring Swiatek to erase a 0-2 deficit and save seven of eight break points before she finally took the lead on her fourth set point.
Upping the pressure with her relentless forehand, Swiatek claimed a 10th game in a row to build a 4-0 advantage in the second set.
The former world number one briefly lost momentum, getting broken by Frech, but recovered to advance to the round of 16, where she awaits one of two lucky losers, Lanlana Tararudee or Ashlyn Krueger.

British world number 170 Sonay Kartal, who missed six months this year with a spinal stress fracture, upset ninth-seeded Belinda Bencic 6-0, 7-5 to book a date with Jasmine Paolini or Nikola Bartunkova.
f866777fd33dd5d2: WASHINGTON, Oct 14 — A federal judge blocked yesterday the White House from banning CNN, MS Now and Politico journalists, following President Donald Trump’s decision to ban the news outlets last month.
District Judge Timothy Kelly ruled that the Trump administration must grant the journalists access to the White House while the lawsuit filed by the three outlets against the ban proceeds.
Kelly said the outlets were “likely to succeed not only on their due process claim, but also on their two First Amendment claims.”
The First Amendment upholds the right to a free press.
Trump barred CNN, MS NOW and Politico from the White House on September 18 for distributing what he called “fake news” and “fiction and lies.”
The three outlets filed a joint lawsuit seeking a preliminary injunction against the ban.
A court order temporarily restored the White House credentials of the journalists. That ban was set to expire yesterday.
“The Court will extend the relief it already ordered, which will continue to preserve the status quo while this case proceeds,” Kelly wrote in an opinion accompanying yesterday’s order.
“President Trump likely banned Plaintiffs from the White House because he believes that their reporting is generally inaccurate and biased against him,” Kelly added.
Trump has long attacked media that have aired critical coverage of him, repeatedly blasting the press as the “enemy of the people.” — AFP
57e25d90d02e7e25: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 14 — Malaysia and Indonesia have begun discussions to explore ways of working together to tackle forest fires in Kalimantan and Sumatra that have caused transboundary haze.

Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan said the discussions involved relevant agencies and ministries from both countries, including the National Disaster Management Agency (Nadma), the Foreign Ministry and the National Security Council (MKN).
“Our secretary-general (Tan Sri Amran Mohamed Zin) has held discussions with MKN, Nadma and the Indonesian side on how we can jointly address these fires. This is the latest development.

“The form of cooperation will depend on the outcome of the discussions, but the authorities of both countries have, for the first time, begun talks on how we can work together to tackle the haze, which appears to be getting worse,” he said.

He was speaking to reporters after attending the handover ceremony for a solar photovoltaic (grid-connected PV) system installation project by the Works Ministry to the Foreign Ministry and three other government premises here today.

He said the discussions marked an initial step by both countries towards finding ways to cooperate in addressing forest fires and the haze, which had persisted for more than a month and was approaching two months.
Mohamad said the prolonged haze had affected not only Malaysia but also threatened the health of people in Indonesia and Singapore.
“Alhamdulillah, both countries, through their respective agencies and foreign ministries, will explore ways to cooperate and help address the forest fires together,” he said.

On Monday, Mohamad was reported as saying that Malaysia would raise the issue of transboundary haze at an Asean Foreign Ministers’ meeting ahead of the bloc’s 49th Summit in Manila next month, to discuss more effective regional mechanisms to tackle the problem. — Bernama
36c2f19feb7f1c93: PETALING JAYA: Seorang lelaki dipenjara lapan tahun enam bulan oleh Mahkamah Tinggi Johor Bahru selepas mengaku bersalah mendera kanak-kanak lelaki berusia tiga tahun hingga menyebabkan kematiannya termasuk memaksa mangsa memakan najis, empat tahun lalu.
Hukuman dijatuhkan oleh Pesuruhjaya Kehakiman Abdul Fareed Abdul Gafoor terhadap tertuduh, Chan Wen Jin, 32, dan mengarahkannya berkuat kuasa dari tarikh tangkapan 3 Okt 2022.
Dia yang juga bekas pemandu e-panggilan dijatuhkan hukuman itu selepas mengaku bersalah terhadap pertuduhan pilihan di bawah Seksyen 31(1) Akta Kanak-kanak 2001.
Mahkamah turut memerintahkan tertuduh melaksanakan bon berkelakuan baik dengan seorang penjamin tanpa cagaran bagi tempoh tiga tahun, menurut Sinar Harian.
Chan turut diarahkan melaksanakan kerja komuniti selama 36 jam dalam tempoh tidak melebihi enam bulan.
Dalam penghakimannya, Fareed berkata hukuman perlu mengimbangi kepentingan awam dan tertuduh, selain mengambil kira keseriusan kesalahan, fakta kes serta faktor mitigasi.

Menurutnya, perbuatan tertuduh yang memaksa mangsa memakan najis sendiri daripada lampin pakai buang sebagai tindakan tidak bertamadun, menjatuhkan maruah dan sama sekali tidak boleh dianggap sebagai kaedah mendidik.

“Rakaman itu menunjukkan perbuatan tertuduh melampaui hukuman fizikal biasa, sebawliknya merupakan penderaan keterlaluan tanpa belas kasihan terhadap kanak-kanak berusia tiga tahun yang tidak berdaya melindungi diri sendiri,” katanya.
Mahkamah menegaskan tertuduh telah mengkhianati kepercayaan bapa mangsa yang mengamanahkannya untuk menjaga kanak-kanak berkenaan.
Abdul Fareed turut menolak hujah pihak pembelaan bahawa perbuatan itu merupakan cara tertuduh mendidik mangsa, seperti yang dilakukannya terhadap anak sendiri.
“Sekiranya tertuduh tidak mampu menjaga mangsa, dia sepatutnya menyerahkan kanak-kanak itu kembali kepada bapanya,” katanya.
Tertuduh sebelum ini didakwa di Mahkamah Majistret Johor Bahru atas pertuduhan membunuh Lee See Jie yang berusia tiga tahun di Skudai, antara 8 malam hingga 8.30 malam pada 2 Okt 2022.
Pertuduhan asal dikemukakan mengikut Seksyen 302 Kanun Keseksaan.
Kes dikendalikan Timbalan Pendakwa Raya Edelynn Wong dan Nur Diana Zubir manakala tertuduh diwakili peguam K Sarawanakumar serta Freeda Sabapathy.
bb7cb5d7e3f7a25e: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 14 — Air quality slipped further this afternoon, with 28 of the country's 68 monitoring stations recording unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings as of 2pm, according to the Department of Environment (DOE).
The unhealthy tally rose from 27 this morning and 20 yesterday. Another 38 stations reported moderate air quality, while two recorded good levels.
Pasir Gudang in Johor logged the nation’s highest reading at 179, leading seven unhealthy stations in the state, including Pengerang (170), Kota Tinggi (168), and Larkin (166).
In the Klang Valley, Klang and peat fire hotspot Johan Setia tied at 175, while Cheras recorded 169, Putrajaya 166, Batu Muda 165, and both Shah Alam and Banting 162.
Elsewhere, Nilai in Negeri Sembilan held at 174, Port Dickson recorded 166, and Seremban stood at 161. All three Melaka stations were unhealthy, led by Bukit Rambai at 173.
On the east of the peninsula, Indera Mahkota in Pahang logged 156, alongside Kemaman (155) and Paka (153) in Terengganu.
In Sarawak, Sri Aman and IPD Serian eased to 126 and 125 respectively.
The persistent haze kept all schools closed today across Johor, Melaka, and Negeri Sembilan, alongside nine education districts in Selangor, Pahang, Sabah, and Sarawak.
1ab9b9ecc8adda75: KUCHING, Oct 14 — Children who do not yet hold Malaysian citizenship remain eligible for access to education at government or government-aided schools if they have at least one biological parent who is a Malaysian citizen, subject to the conditions and procedures of the Education Ministry (MOE).

Sarawak Minister of Women, Childhood and Community Wellbeing Development Datuk Seri Fatimah Abdullah said this eligibility is governed by the Education Act 1996 (Act 550), the Education Regulations 1998 and MOE procedures currently in force.
“For the purpose of school admission, information on the biological parent who is a Malaysian citizen must be stated in the child’s birth certificate.
“Citizenship status and access to education are two separate matters,” she said during the question-and-answer session at the Sarawak State Legislative Assembly sitting here today.

She was responding to a question from Dr Johnichal Rayong Ngipa (GPS-Engkilili) on the status of children with a non-citizen parent but who were born and raised in Sarawak, as well as their eligibility to attend school.
Meanwhile, she said records from the National Registration Department (JPN) showed that 224 children born in Sarawak were registered as non-citizens between January and August this year.
“Among the main factors causing children to be registered as non-citizens or issued pink birth certificates are their parents’ marriages not registered or not recognised under Malaysian law.
“Other factors include mothers without valid identification documents, as well as cases of children who were found abandoned,” she said in reply to a supplementary question from Dr Rayong.
She said the state government is stepping up efforts to reduce the problem, including holding dialogues with communities and running awareness campaigns to encourage lawful marriage registration.

In addition, assistance will be given to mothers born in Sarawak but lacking identification documents to obtain such documents through the channels and procedures set out under the Sarawak Births and Deaths Registration Ordinance (Chapter 10). — Bernama
d05546d4ddcf709e: BEIJING, Oct 14 — China’s exports soared in September, official data showed today, putting the country on course for a record annual trade surplus that is likely to increase calls for rebalancing trade from major partners, including the European Union and the United States.
Exports rose 36.3 per cent year-on-year according to China’s customs administration, far exceeding the 25.7 per cent rise predicted by a Bloomberg survey of analysts.
Imports also spiked 31 per cent in September, but the world’s second-largest economy still recorded a trade surplus of US$133.5 billion (RM545 billion), the largest monthly figure since January 2025.
China’s cumulative trade surplus through the end of September reached US$938.1 billion, putting it on course to break the record US$1.2 trillion surplus it recorded last year.
With domestic demand weak by comparison — retail sales grew just 0.4 per cent on-year in August — Beijing has relied on exports to meet its annual growth target of 4.5 to 5 per cent.
But the boom in shipments has triggered pushback from major markets including the United States — which launched a bruising trade war against China last year — and Europe.
Shipments to the US rose 39.6 per cent in September, up from a low base last year when trade cratered after Beijing and Washington slapped punitive tariffs on each others’ goods.
Shipments to the EU rose 25.3 per cent in September, while imports from the 27-nation bloc were flat, pushing China’s trade surplus with the bloc to new heights.
EU officials have described the bloc’s deficit with China, which runs at more than 1 billion euros a day, as “unsustainable” and pledged to rebalance the trading relationship.

Talks last week between China and EU trade chiefs Maros Sefcovic and Wang Wentao ended with an agreement to limit exports of Chinese hybrid vehicles to Europe, though analysts say that makes up only a small share of bilateral trade.

“Brussels is considering expanding restrictions to more strategic sectors, though we estimate that the impact of this on China’s economy would be small,” said Nguyen Hoang Nam, China economist at Capital Economics. — AFP

d0dbb75b6c691c48: THE HAGUE: Dutch tech giant ASML, which makes cutting-edge machines to manufacture semiconductor chips, Wednesday posted a gain in third-quarter net profits compared with the same period in 2025.
ASML, Europe's biggest tech firm by market value, said net profits came in at €5.0 billion, compared with €2.1 billion in the third quarter of last year.
The firm also hiked its full-year sales forecast, predicting total turnover of between €44-€45 billion, from a previous projection of €43-€45 billion.
ASML is a critical cog in the global economy and a key bellwether for the tech sector, as the semiconductors crafted with its tools power everything from smartphones to missiles.
It has also become a pivotal player in AI, as the only manufacturer of machines high tech enough to provide the advanced chips for AI systems worldwide.

"Our customers continue to increase their short- and medium-term equipment demand forecasts with us, driven primarily by their views on the size and duration of AI-related investments," said the firm's chief executive Christophe Fouquet.
"In light of their demand visibility, some customers are expressing an interest in placing orders with us for 2029 and even 2030," he added.
He said that demand was currently outstripping supply and that the firm was seeking ways to boost its capacity for 2028 beyond a 30% increase the firm had already announced.
ac551ce98e1ecdf4: PETALING JAYA: A former e-hailing driver was sentenced to eight years and six months’ imprisonment by the Johor Bahru High Court today after pleading guilty to abusing a three-year-old boy in 2022, including forcing him to eat his own faeces.

Utusan Malaysia reported that Chan Wen Jie, 32, pleaded guilty to an alternative charge of child abuse under Section 31(1)(a) of the Child Act 2001 before judicial commissioner Abdul Fareed Abdul Gafoor.

The father of two was ordered to serve his prison sentence from the date of his arrest on Oct 3, 2022 and complete 36 hours of community service within six months. He was also placed on a three-year good behaviour bond.
In his judgment, Fareed condemned Chan’s actions which were captured on CCTV camera, and rejected the defence’s argument that Chan had merely been disciplining the boy.
"The accused not only caned the victim but also slapped him, hit him on the head and forced him to do squats, stand for long periods and eat his faeces from his disposable diaper.

"Forcing the child to eat faeces was a cruel and degrading act that could in no way be considered a form of discipline. If the accused was unable to care for the victim, he should have handed the child back to his father," he said.
Chan was charged in the Johor Bahru magistrates’ court in 2022 with murdering Lee See Jie, 3, at a house on Jalan Ria 2 in Taman Skudai Ria, Skudai, between 8pm and 8.30pm on Oct 2.
The charge, which was later withdrawn, was brought under Section 302 of the Penal Code, which provides for the death penalty or 30 to 40 years’ imprisonment and at least 12 strokes of the rotan.
The Star reported Fareed as saying the High Court did not consider the original murder charge or the cause of the victim’s death when determining the sentence for the alternative charge.
The court ruled that the jail term was appropriate for the offence after weighing aggravating and mitigating factors.
The prosecution was led by deputy public prosecutors Edelynn Wong and Nur Diyana Zubir, while Chan was represented by K Sarawanakumar and Freda Sabapathy.
3074fdf56d1f1712: WASHINGTON, Oct 14 — US President Donald Trump posted disturbing footage on his Truth Social account yesterday of a man being fatally mauled by a tiger in Britain, sparking backlash on social media.
The 41-second clip of the UK man being attacked Saturday in a wildlife park was also later shared by the White House’s “Rapid Response 47” account on X.

Trump, who regularly posts provocative material on social media, followed up his initial post — which he captioned “Don’t ever mess with nature!” — with a video clip of apparently AI-generated visuals of individuals being mauled by big cats to the tune of a tinny synthesiser.
Users on X, where the “Rapid Response 47” account has 2.3 million followers, questioned the president’s judgment, with one calling the post “sick.”
“I’m a big supporter but not a fan of this post. To each his own,” wrote another.
Later yesterday, Trump doubled down and posted an AI generated video of himself wrestling and befriending the smiling tiger, to the tune of “The Lion Sleeps Tonight.”
The man in the real video, identified by the BBC as William Chapman, later died from his injuries following the Saturday incident, police said.
British police responded to reports of a man entering the enclosure at the Yorkshire Wildlife Park, near the northern city of Doncaster.
“The tiger subsequently attacked the man, resulting in serious injury,” police said in a statement.
“Emergency services attended and sadly, despite the best efforts of medical personnel, the man was pronounced dead at the scene,” it added.
Yorkshire Ambulance Service said it had sent two ambulances by road and an air ambulance to the scene.
The park’s “Land of the Tigers” feature has a 300-meter raised walkway.
From the walkway, visitors can view the park’s Amur tigers in their enclosure which includes woodland, grassland and a waterfall pool.
There are estimated to be only around 500 of the endangered subspecies left in the wild. — AFP

39fd132af63cde94: KUALA LUMPUR: Kerajaan digesa membatalkan cadangan syarat simpanan minimum RM15,000 dalam akaun khas Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH) kerana dikhuatiri membebankan golongan berpendapatan rendah, khususnya penduduk luar bandar.

Tuan Ibrahim Tuan Man (PN-Kubang Kerian) berkata syarat itu tidak semestinya mencerminkan kemampuan sebenar bakal jemaah, malah menyukarkan pasangan suami isteri yang perlu menyediakan simpanan berjumlah RM30,000.
"30,000 ini bagi orang kampung satu jumlah yang sangat besar. Kalau dah senaraikan mereka dapat pergi haji, mereka memang dah persiapkan duit.
"Tapi nak masukkan RM30,000 dalam akaun sampai pergi haji, apa mekanisme yang dibuat?" katanya ketika membahaskan Belanjawan 2027 di Dewan Rakyat.
Timbalan presiden PAS itu turut menggesa TH kembali kepada matlamat asal penubuhannya, iaitu memudahkan umat Islam menunaikan ibadah haji, bukannya menambah beban kewangan bakal jemaah.
"Asal usul Tabung Haji diwujudkan ialah untuk memudahkan umat Islam pergi haji. Hari ini ia dah jadi entiti bisnes dan beban dikembalikan kepada jemaah," katanya.
Beliau turut mengambil contoh Mara, Felcra dan Risda yang menurutnya pernah menceburi bidang di luar fungsi asal penubuhan sehingga ada kolej terpaksa ditutup.
Isu syarat simpanan minimum itu turut dibangkitkan Ketua Pembangkang Hamzah Zainudin di Dewan Rakyat, Isnin lalu.
Hamzah dilaporkan bimbang kira-kira tiga juta pendeposit sedia ada mungkin terkeluar daripada senarai giliran haji sekiranya syarat berkenaan dilaksanakan.
Sebelum ini, media melaporkan lebih 80% daripada kira-kira 4.1 juta pendeposit yang mendaftar untuk menunaikan haji masih belum mencapai jumlah simpanan minimum RM15,000.
Menteri di Jabatan Perdana Menteri (Hal Ehwal Agama) Dr Zulkifli Hasan berkata keadaan itu menunjukkan pentingnya pendeposit TH membuat persediaan kewangan lebih awal.
Langkah menetapkan syarat itu dibuat untuk memastikan kemampuan kewangan serta penolakan atau penangguhan tawaran.

9b4b0fd2828cece9: SEOUL: Former US vice president Kamala Harris urged governments and technology companies on Wednesday to urgently put safeguards in place for artificial intelligence, warning that the window for containing its gravest risks was closing.
"If we are to have any guardrails and safeguards, they have to be at the table," Harris said of AI developers during an appearance at South Korea's Asan Institute for Policy Studies.
"My concern is that the window is shutting."

Harris said governments and companies must act immediately against what she described as three existential dangers from AI - cybersecurity threats, AI-enabled weapons and systems escaping human control.
She also urged the US to engage China on international rules and standards for AI, saying their broader strategic rivalry should not preclude cooperation on shared risks.
"There is room for cooperation where our interests are aligned," Harris said, calling for "healthy and robust competition, but not conflict."
Harris criticised what she called US president Donald Trump's "erratic tariffs" and their punitive nature, before warning against a transactional approach that cost the US global influence.
"The question is, are we thinking only about the short term, or do we also value and appreciate the significance of an investment for long-term gain?"
Harris praised South Korean investment in US shipbuilding, semiconductors, electric vehicles and clean energy, calling it "immensely significant and valued".
She also called for renewed US commitment to South Korea, saying growing cooperation among North Korea, Russia, China and Iran was very concerning and meant the allies must strengthen deterrence.
The former vice president has been campaigning for Democratic candidates ahead of the 2026 US midterm elections as she weighs another White House bid.

She said Democrats would win a majority in the House of Representatives and had a "very good shot" at taking the Senate, potentially giving Congress a stronger voice on domestic and foreign policy, including the war with Iran.
Asked whether she would again seek the presidency in 2028, Harris said: "I'm still thinking about it. I haven’t decided yet."
9cdd485dd74012fd: PETALING JAYA: Seorang bekas pemimpin Umno mencadangkan semua gabungan dan parti politik bertanding secara solo pada PRN Melaka bagi mengukur kekuatan sebenar masing-masing menjelang PRU16 akan datang.

Bekas Ahli Parlimen Batu Pahat, Puad Zarkashi, berkata parti-parti utama dilihat menghadapi kesukaran untuk bertolak ansur dan mencapai persetujuan mengenai kerjasama politik bagi PRN pada 14 Nov ini.
"Lebih baik semua gabungan sama ada Barisan Nasional (BN), Pakatan Harapan (PH), PAS, Bersatu, Wawasan atau Bersama bertanding secara solo. Lihat kekuatan masing masing bila bertanding solo.
"Baru nampak siapa perlukan siapa. Siapa kalau tanding sendiri baru tahu parti itu hanyalah parti nyamuk.
"Maka barulah di PRU 16 nanti ada rasa rendah diri, sedia mendongak langit dalam menentukan rakan kongsi yang lebih realistik,” katanya dalam hantaran di Facebook.

Pengundi Melaka akan keluar mengundi pada 14 Nov ini, dengan 28 kerusi dipertandingkan. BN memenangi 21 kerusi pada PRN 2021, manakala PH memperoleh lima kerusi dan Perikatan Nasional (PN) dua kerusi.
BN sebelum ini menyatakan hasrat untuk bekerjasama dengan PN di Melaka susulan kemenangan besar gabungan mereka pada PRN Negeri Sembilan 1 Ogos lalu.
Bagaimanapun, gabungan pimpinan Umno itu membuka ruang rundingan dengan PH dan mengambil masa untuk mengesahkan kerjasama dengan PN pimpinan PAS.
Presiden PAS Abdul Hadi Awang bagaimanapun mendakwa PAS dan BN pada dasarnya sudah bersetuju untuk bergabung tenaga di Melaka.
Sementara itu, PH dikaitkan dengan spekulasi mengenai kemungkinan pakatan dengan Bersatu, yang semakin tersisih dalam PN meskipun masih menjadi komponen gabungan pembangkang itu.
2661e37ee31db8d5: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 14 — His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, today received a courtesy visit from Melaka Yang di-Pertua Negeri Tun Mohd Ali Mohd Rustam at Istana Negara in Kuala Lumpur.
The meeting took place before His Majesty attended the 273rd Conference of Rulers.
The 273rd Conference of Rulers is chaired by the Sultan of Perak, Sultan Nazrin Muizzuddin Shah.
2c084e8e2b210c47: NEW DELHI, Oct 14 — Two top leaders of India’s youth-led Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) were sent to jail for five days today for alleged trespassing, the party said.
Ashutosh Ranka and Saurav Das “have been sent to five days judicial custody”, CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke said in a social media post.

Das and Ranka were detained yesterday for entering Jantar Mantar, a day after Delhi Police announced that the Jantar Mantar street in the heart of the capital had been taken off the list of designated official protest sites.

A video posted online by Dipke yesterday showed the duo clambering over barricades at Jantar Mantar street, running into an empty space and waving the national flag — before police chased and detained them.

Supporters of the online movement and opposition parties have taken to the streets in recent days, demanding the resignation of the head of India’s election commission, accusing it of manipulating voter rolls to benefit Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s ruling party.
The Election Commission of India, which oversees the voting process in the world’s most populous nation, has denied any wrongdoing.
The site has been sealed off for several days by yellow metal barricades and guarded by a heavy police presence.
Dipke today defended Das and Ranka, saying they were being punished just for “unfurling tricolour at Jantar Mantar.
693435a901dc8b1e: PETALING JAYA: Persatuan Hak Asasi Manusia Kebangsaan, atau Hakam, menggesa tindakan kumpulan tertentu yang menyasarkan pelarian Rohingya dihentikan susulan peningkatan sentimen xenofobia dan permusuhan terhadap komuniti itu.

Presiden Hakam, M Ramachelvam, melahirkan kebimbangan terhadap tindakan orang awam mengambil tindakan terhadap pelarian termasuk kes semalam di mana beberapa rumah Rohingya di Johor di baling bom petrol.
Ramachelvam berkata tindakan itu membelakangkan kedaulatan undang-undang, meningkatkan risiko keganasan dan menggalakkan sikap menyalahkan seluruh komuniti secara kolektif.

“Tindakan ugutan dan keganasan itu mesti dikutuk tanpa sebarang keraguan, manakala sebarang rungutan mesti ditangani melalui proses yang sah di sisi undang-undang dan bukannya tindakan balas secara sendirian.

“Apabila perbuatan sedemikian ditujukan kepada komuniti etnik atau pelarian, ia turut mewujudkan persekitaran yang memungkinkan sikap menyalahkan seluruh komuniti secara kolektif dan penyahinsanan dianggap sebagai sesuatu yang boleh diterima.

“Tiada komuniti sepatutnya terpaksa hidup dalam ancaman dan keselamatan mereka bergantung pada ihsan orang yang tidak dikenali, yang mengambil keputusan sendiri untuk menentukan siapa yang layak mendapat perlindungan,” katanya dalam satu kenyataan.
Polis berkata beberapa rumah yang didiami pelarian Rohingya di Kulai, Johor, diserang menggunakan bom petrol (Molotov cocktail) pada tengah malam semalam.
Siasatan mendapati kejadian itu dipercayai sebagai tindak balas terhadap dua video tular yang didakwa menunjukkan sekumpulan lelaki Rohingya mencabar orang ramai untuk bergaduh di Kulai.
Ramachelvam menggesa orang ramai tidak mengambil tindakan sendiri, tidak menyebarkan dakwaan menghasut atau belum disahkan, serta melaporkan kesalahan melalui saluran undang-undang yang betul.
c59dd1afe998d4f4: PETALING JAYA: A former Umno leader has suggested that all political coalitions and parties go solo in the Melaka polls to gauge their actual strength ahead of the next general election (GE16).
Former Batu Pahat MP Puad Zarkashi said it appeared that the major players were struggling to reach a compromise and agree on alliances for the Nov 14 state election.
"It would be better for all of them to go solo, whether Barisan Nasional, Pakatan Harapan, PAS, Bersatu, Wawasan or Bersama, to gauge their respective strengths.
"Only then can they determine who really needs whom, and which entities are merely mosquito parties.
"That way, when GE16 comes along, the relevant parties will be more humble and realistic when choosing their electoral partners," Puad said in a Facebook post.
Voters in Melaka will go to the polls on Nov 14, with 28 seats up for grabs. BN won 21 seats in the 2021 polls, while PH secured five and Perikatan Nasional two.
BN previously stated its intention to cooperate with PN in Melaka following their alliance's convincing victory in the Aug 1 Negeri Sembilan polls.
However, the Umno-led coalition opened the door to talks with PH and dragged its feet in confirming an alliance with PAS-led PN.
PAS president Abdul Hadi Awang nonetheless claimed that PAS and BN had agreed in principle to join forces in Melaka.
PH, meanwhile, has been linked to speculation of a pact with Bersatu, which fell out of favour in PN but remains a component of the opposition coalition.
e803dd0b2c6e32fd: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 14 — Thick smoke seen near the Duta-Ulu Kelang Expressway (DUKE), beyond the Sentul Toll Plaza on Wednesday, is believed to have been caused by a burning streetlight.

Sentul district police chief Assistant Commissioner Anuar Bakri Abdul Salam said inspections by police and DUKE highway management found that the smoke originated from a streetlight that had caught fire, according to a report by Sinar Harian.
“The fire was successfully extinguished and the incident did not involve any injuries or loss of life.
“Inspection findings showed that the smoke came from a burning streetlight and the fire was successfully extinguished,” he said in a statement on Wednesday.
A video showing thick smoke engulfing the area near the highway had earlier gone viral on social media.
The footage also showed several vehicles, including motorcycles, passing through the area.
Social media users had claimed that the smoke was coming from a drain near the highway, although its actual source had not been established at the time.
Anuar Bakri said the incident occurred at Ramp 0.5, along the route from Greenwood towards the exit leading to Kuala Lumpur Hospital (HKL).
He added that DUKE highway management was still handling follow-up action over the incident.
d15291e2fdbf074c: BEIJING: China's exports soared in September, official data showed Wednesday, putting the country on course for a record annual trade surplus that is likely to increase calls for rebalancing trade from major partners, including the European Union (EU) and the US.
Exports rose 36.3% year-on-year according to China's customs administration, far exceeding the 25.7% rise predicted by a Bloomberg survey of analysts.
Imports also spiked 31% in September, but the world's second-largest economy still recorded a trade surplus of US$133.5 billion, the largest monthly figure since January 2025.
China's cumulative trade surplus through the end of September reached US$938.1 billion, putting it on course to break the record US$1.2 trillion surplus it recorded last year.
With domestic demand weak by comparison -- retail sales grew just 0.4% year-on-year in August -- Beijing has relied on exports to meet its annual growth target of 4.5% to 5%.
But the boom in shipments has triggered pushback from major markets including the US -- which launched a bruising trade war against China last year -- and Europe.
Shipments to the US rose 39.6% in September, up from a low base last year when trade cratered after Beijing and Washington slapped punitive tariffs on each others' goods.
Shipments to the EU rose 25.3% in September, while imports from the 27-nation bloc were flat, pushing China's trade surplus with the bloc to new heights.
EU officials have described the bloc's deficit with China, which runs at more than 1 billion euros a day, as "unsustainable" and pledged to rebalance the trading relationship.

Talks last week between China and EU trade chiefs Maros Sefcovic and Wang Wentao ended with an agreement to limit exports of Chinese hybrid vehicles to Europe, though analysts say that makes up only a small share of bilateral trade.

"Brussels is considering expanding restrictions to more strategic sectors, though we estimate that the impact of this on China's economy would be small," said Nguyen Hoang Nam, China economist at Capital Economics.

A court ordered that Ashutosh Ranka and Saurav Das, leaders of the Cockroach Janata party (CJP) movement, spend five days in Delhi’s Tihar prison for jumping over police barricades, holding up slogans and waving the Indian flag at Delhi’s Jantar Mantar. 0ea4acebf2015841: DUBLIN: Google announced Wednesday that it will open up its most advanced artificial intelligence models to 200 European researchers.

"By delivering vital compute power and state-of-the-art tools directly to research teams, this effort aims to accelerate the pace of European innovation and reinforce the continent's scientific competitiveness," Google said in a statement released at an AI summit in Dublin.

The researchers, chosen by the European Commission under its Resource for AI Science in Europe (RAISE) scheme, will get access to Google DeepMind and Google Cloud's "leading scientific tools including AlphaFold 3, WeatherNext, AlphaGenome, AlphaEvolve, and AlphaEarth Foundations," Google said.
AlphaFold 3 specialises in research on proteins while WeatherNext specialises in meteorological forecasts.
The announcement came as demands for greater regulation of AI have increased following a series of security incidents.
dfb335da48ffb16b: KUALA LUMPUR: Kerajaan Persekutuan digesa memperincikan pecahan peruntukan RM18.7 bilion untuk Sabah dalam Belanjawan 2027 mengikut kementerian supaya rakyat dapat mengetahui jumlah sebenar yang disalurkan bagi pembangunan negeri itu.

Isnaraissah Munirah Majilis (Warisan-Kota Belud) berkata jumlah diumumkan itu bukan semuanya untuk pembangunan kerana turut merangkumi belanja mengurus, termasuk pembayaran gaji kakitangan Persekutuan yang bertugas di Sabah.

Katanya, perbelanjaan mengurus sememangnya tanggungjawab kerajaan Persekutuan di semua negeri dan tidak sepatutnya menimbulkan gambaran bahawa keseluruhan RM18.7 bilion diperuntukkan khusus untuk pembangunan Sabah.
“Sebenarnya dari dulu pun belanja operasi di bawah tanggungjawab Persekutuan dan bukan Sabah sahaja yang kena bayar, negeri-negeri lain juga.
“Dan kena maklum bahawa ini tiada kaitan dengan 40%,” katanya merujuk kepada pemberian khas berdasarkan hasil diperoleh dari wilayah Sabah.
Beliau berkata demikian pada perbahasan Belanjawan 2027 di Dewan Rakyat.
Dalam Belanjawan 2027, Perdana Menteri Anwar Ibrahim mengumumkan peningkatan peruntukan Persekutuan untuk Sabah kepada RM18.7 bilion berbanding RM17.6 bilion tahun ini.

Dalam pada itu, beliau berkata, analisis terhadap Buku Anggaran Perbelanjaan Persekutuan dan Penyata Kewangan Kerajaan Persekutuan bagi 2023 hingga 2025 menunjukkan jurang ketara antara peruntukan asal dengan perbelanjaan yang dapat dikenal pasti.
Menurutnya, daripada RM19.8 bilion yang diumumkan untuk Sabah sepanjang tempoh itu, hanya RM4.22 bilion perbelanjaan dapat dikesan secara khusus menerusi butiran dalam dokumen rasmi berkenaan.

“Malah dalam tempoh 2023 hingga 2024 sahaja, lebih RM1.83 bilion peruntukan khusus Sabah telah dikurangkan dalam tahun semasa, manakala melebihi RM1.9 bilion yang diumumkan gagal dibelanjakan,” katanya.

Isnaraissah mendakwa pemotongan peruntukan pada pertengahan tahun juga membolehkan sesetengah kementerian mencatat pencapaian petunjuk prestasi utama (KPI) yang tinggi dari segi peratusan, walaupun pelaksanaan pembangunan infrastruktur asas terjejas.
Beliau turut meminta penyata perbelanjaan sebenar Kerajaan Persekutuan di Sabah yang diaudit Ketua Audit Negara dibentangkan setiap tahun di Parlimen dan DUN Sabah.

Katanya, baki peruntukan yang diluluskan untuk Sabah tidak sepatutnya dipindahkan keluar, sebaliknya digunakan bagi membiayai projek infrastruktur atau kemudahan asas lain yang masih diperlukan rakyat negeri itu.
a7f8bf26ed931a9c: PETALING JAYA: The National Human Rights Society (Hakam) has warned against vigilantism against Rohingya refugees amid concerns of growing xenophobia and hostility towards the community.

Hakam president M Ramachelvam expressed concern over members of the public acting as self-appointed enforcers against refugees, including a case yesterday where several Rohingya homes in Johor were firebombed.
Ramachelvam said such behaviour undermined the rule of law, increased the risk of violence and encouraged collective blame against entire communities.
"Such acts of intimidation and violence must be unequivocally condemned, and grievances must be addressed through lawful processes rather than private acts of retaliation.
"When such conduct is directed at an ethnic or refugee community, it also creates an environment in which collective blame and dehumanisation can be treated as acceptable.

"No community should have to live under the threat that its safety depends on the goodwill of strangers who have taken it upon themselves to determine who deserves protection," he said in a statement.
Police revealed that several houses inhabited by Rohingya refugees in Kulai, Johor, were attacked with Molotov cocktails past midnight yesterday.
Investigations suggested that the incident was in response to two viral videos purportedly showing a group of Rohingya men daring people to a fight in Kulai.
Ramachelvam urged the public to reject vigilantism, refrain from spreading inflammatory or unverified allegations, and report suspected offences through the appropriate legal channels.
a1313fd9ed5df739: SEOUL: South Korea's football association has told fans to stop "excessive personal attacks", warning of the "psychological burden" it could inflict on national team players in the crosshairs since their World Cup flop.
Hong Myung-bo quit as coach after the team failed to advance past the group stage in North America, and Spanish interim Robert Moreno is awaiting word on a possible extension.
With the Asian Cup scheduled to take place in January in Saudi Arabia, the national side are engulfed by claims of internal divisions.
Local media reports say some younger players feel held back by senior members of the squad, including long-time captain Son Heung-min.
In a lengthy statement, the Korea Football Association condemned what it called attempts to sow discord.

"Unverified information and speculative claims about national football team players have recently been spreading on social media and online forums, with some players facing excessive criticism and personal attacks," the KFA said on Tuesday.

"Such behaviour goes beyond the bounds of legitimate criticism and can place a severe psychological burden on individual players," it said, urging fans to refrain from "making assumptions about internal team dynamics and fuelling divisions within the squad".

Speculation about discord emerged after Bayern Munich defender Kim Min-jae threw his boots in anger after being substituted in the second half of the disappointing home 0-0 draw with Venezuela this month.
Kim said afterwards that "every player needs to put their head down and give it their all", fuelling talk of divisions within the squad.
The latest firestorm follows public outrage over the behaviour of some players who earned exemptions from mandatory military service after winning gold at the Asian Games.

Their post-match celebrations, seen as suggesting that military exemptions had been their main motivation, sparked a backlash and prompted defence minister Kang Shin-chul to pledge to scale back the benefit.
9f10fe09f54eb3e8: PETALING JAYA: The Kota Kinabalu coroner’s court heard today that the officer investigating Zara Qairina Mahathir’s death only knew of two internal investigations conducted by the school’s disciplinary unit, following earlier testimony that the unit conducted five without informing the police.
Wong Yew Zhung told coroner Amir Shah Amir Hassan that he only knew of the internal investigations conducted on July 17 and 18, 2025.
"I know this because I was given five statements from senior students," he was quoted as saying by Borneo Post.
On Nov 27 last year, assistant chief discipline teacher Nurul Syahadah Ibrahim testified that five internal probes were conducted on July 16, July 17, Aug 4, Aug 5 and Aug 13.
She said the students’ written statements were not given to the police, who only received statements from the five students accused of verbally abusing Zara.
Nurul said the school’s disciplinary unit continued its internal investigations for record-keeping purposes after police took over the investigation on July 16.
Zara died at Queen Elizabeth Hospital on July 17, 2025, a day after she was found unconscious near a drain at her school dormitory in the early morning.
Her remains were exhumed on Aug 9, and a post-mortem examination was conducted at the hospital’s forensic medicine department on Aug 10.
On Aug 20, five minors, given the pseudonyms Students A, B, C, D and E, were charged in the Kota Kinabalu children's court with verbally abusing Zara.

f833587b60d69429: Tom Watson has said ‘mob rule’ must not decide public contracts. Perhaps he should take a look at his new employer What a world we live in. Well, OK, it might not have happened yet, but it’s only a matter of time. ca378f8ba8e7d551: Tim Beasley, a senior incident response consultant at Semperis, was investigating a cyberattack involving Russia’s Midnight Blizzard when a package containing nesting dolls and other regional gifts showed up on his doorstep. At the time, Beasley served as the lead investigator for Microsoft’s Detection and Response Team (DART). He assumed it was from the group, which has been linked to the Kremlin’s Foreign Intelligence Service (SVR), although the sender didn’t leave a note. “Just little souvenirs and gift basket stuff from that area of the world,” he told The Register. “We-know-where-you-are kind of stuff. It’s a real eye-opener when you get that type of thing.” While digital intrusions having physical consequences is nothing new, cybercriminals in recent years have turned to real-life harm and mental and physical trauma to force victims into paying extortion demands. Some groups even use cybercrime as a gateway drug to real-life violence. Over the summer, Europol and its partners' investigators flagged 4,340 “horrific” URLs for removal as part of an ongoing crackdown on The Com (short for community), a loosely knit network of online groups whose young members participate in a range of illicit activities including hacking, swatting, digital extortion, real-life shootings, and other physical violence. “We’ve seen violence as a service get used,” Beasley said. He’s also investigated ransomware attacks where C-suite executives receive pictures of their kids’ schools directly from the cybercriminals in an attempt to apply psychological pressure to pay the extortion fee. “I've seen threats involving people's families, from social media reconnaissance, and in our world you more and more come to expect it, which is unfortunate,” Beasley said. This type of psychological intimidation and harm against victim companies’ employees has seen an uptick in the last several years to the point where it's almost common. Thirty-seven percent of ransomware attacks involved psychological or physical threats against staff, according to Semperis’ annual ransomware risk report. The global study of 1,200 post-ransomware organizations conducted over the first half of the year found attackers threatening psychological intimidation (23 percent) and physical threats (17 percent), to force payment. They are not only targeting executives and staff, but also families of their victims. A quarter of these victims experienced doxxing – posting individuals' personal details, such as names, home and work addresses, and phone numbers online – while another 25 percent had to seek psychological and/or medical treatment in response to ransomware infections. Nearly the same number (24 percent) hired personal security teams, while 23 percent experienced swatting calls – that's when attackers phone emergency services and report a bogus incident like a bomb or active-shooter threat to trigger an armed response. Additionally, more than half (53 percent) of respondents reported that ransomware attackers carried through on threats in the past year. Some of these threats reported by ransomed organizations’ employees include: threatening texts, letters, or packages: 57 percent threats against family or friends: 37 percent physical intrusion: 19 percent abduction: 17 percent bodily harm: 13 percent stalking: 6 percent. “It's the more well-known groups,” using psychological and physical threats to force payments, Beasley said. “I've seen Scattered Spider, I've seen ShinyHunters, I've seen Lapsus$.” For what it's worth, ShinyHunters claimed in an exclusive interview with The Register that they “don't attack human beings.” They did, however, admit that “there are times in the work we do sometimes we have to push the corporate to the absolute limit to get them on the table.” The takeaway for defenders and executives from this report is to “stand your ground,” Beasley said. “Don’t buckle under the pressure, and just know that you know it's going to be okay. If you feel like you're under duress, then by all means get law enforcement involved. Don't be afraid to call the cops. Don't be afraid to get the FBI involved, sooner rather than later. And don’t pay them.” This last piece of advice is important, as once you pay, they're going to come back for more. Semperis’ report found that 69 percent of surveyed ransomware victims were targeted multiple times within the past 12 months, and 31 percent made multiple payments to attackers. “Don’t pay anything,” Beasley said. “Never pay them.”®
cc9839dc6d726f77: JERUSALEM: Liran Naaman said he spent 800 euros (nearly US$900) to fly from Amsterdam, where he has lived for the past 11 years, to his native Israel, all to vote in the Oct 27 election.

He has returned to vote in every election except during the Covid-19 pandemic, and believes this time his participation matters more than ever. "The way that our government is conducting itself is harming me personally and the rest of the Israelis abroad," the project manager told AFP.
The election is widely seen as a referendum on Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and his hard-right government after nearly three years of war in Gaza, Iran and Lebanon. Polls show a tight race.

Israel is one of a handful of democracies that does not allow citizens to vote if they are abroad. The influx of overseas voters has alarmed Netanyahu's bloc, mindful of how tens of thousands of Israelis, disgruntled during his latest tenure, have left the country.
More than 50,000 Israelis are expected to travel home to cast their ballots, according to the Aid Coalition, a US-based NGO that advocates for Israeli democracy.
For Sylvie Lidgi, a dual French-Israeli national, the country stands at a crossroads between "two opposing visions of the world: either the Torah (Bible) as a constitution, or a liberal democracy".
"That's why I'm going to vote," the Parisian pensioner told AFP, noting that the last time she cast a ballot in Israel was in 1973.
Since then, she had felt it inappropriate to vote while living abroad. "But this year, it's really different," she said. "It's about values."
Crucial time' for Israel
The relationship between religion and state is also a decisive factor for Tami Giniger, a startup consultant who will fly home from Bangkok to vote.
"This is a crucial time... for defining what is Israeli, what is Judaism, how these things work together," she said.
"I do love that (Israel) is a Jewish state. But I don't think that it needs to be fanatic," she added.

The Aid Coalition has launched a non-partisan initiative, called Fly & Vote, to assist Israelis abroad who want to return for the election. The programme provides information on the location of polling stations and identification requirements.
It also helps arrange travel by purchasing seats on commercial flights and reselling them, and in some cases has chartered aircraft.
Likud, Netanyahu's party, filed a petition with Israel's Central Elections Committee in early September, accusing the initiative of electoral bribery.
Aid Coalition president Jonathan Barsade told AFP the accusation had "no foundation whatsoever" and that the NGO does not provide financial incentives.
A settlement reached last week requires the NGO to stop selling additional flights as part of the programme, while allowing previously purchased tickets to remain valid.
You need to suffer with us

While some Israelis abroad argue they should be allowed to vote at embassies, Naaman says he appreciates the requirement to return home and experience the country's reality before deciding how to vote.
"Being in Israel gives a very different perspective than being abroad," he said.
"When my family and friends come to visit (in Amsterdam), they're always afraid that Europe has fallen and that everything has become horrible in Europe," he said.
"And when I'm talking to them, I feel like (they) have Iranian missiles every Tuesday and Wednesday!" he said.
Relatives have criticised him for remaining abroad during the war while returning to vote for the country's future.
"You need to be here and suffer with us in order to gain that privilege," he said, describing their message to him.
Yet interviewees said Israeli politics continues to affect them deeply, despite the distance.
Giniger said she felt a "responsibility" to influence through her vote how "Jews and Israelis are perceived in the world today" at a time of rising antisemitism.
National elections, she argued, will shape Israel's relations with the rest of the world.
"Those alliances and the way that the world sees us are crucial to us."
Ariella Hanker, 44, a cancer research scientist in Dallas, was born in Israel to American parents. An observant Jew, she grew up in the US but has always felt strong ties to her country of birth.
After Netanyahu returned to power in 2022 and his government sought to advance a widely criticised judicial overhaul, she resolved to return for the next election.
"I don't know that my vote really will affect anything," she said. "But it's more a personal thing. I don't want to be complacent."
"I'm just really worried about the future of a strong, democratic Israel. And I don't want to blame myself for its downfall. I want to tell myself I did what I could to prevent it."
fa3a0350e4cb2241: PETALING JAYA: Ketua Pemuda Umno Dr Akmal Saleh membayangkan kemungkinan meninggalkan DUN Merlimau untuk bertanding di kerusi lain pada PRN Melaka 14 Nov ini.
Dalam hantaran di Facebook, Akmal merakamkan penghargaan kepada pengundi di Merlimau kerana memilihnya pada PRN 2021, sekali gus memberikannya penggal pertama sebagai wakil rakyat.
"Selepas ini ke mana? Kalau ke Serkam atau Sungai Rambai boleh ke? Atau ada cadangan lain?," katanya.

Sungai Rambai dan Serkam merupakan kubu kuat Umno yang tidak pernah terlepas daripada genggaman parti itu, namun Barisan Nasional (BN) mengekalkan kerusi Serkam dengan majoriti yang amat tipis pada 2021.
BN memenangi kerusi Serkam dalam pertandingan empat penjuru, menewaskan calon Perikatan Nasional (PN) dengan majoriti 79 undi, manakala calon Pakatan Harapan (PH) dan calon bebas ketinggalan jauh.
Akmal dipilih sebagai Adun Merlimau pada 2021 dengan majoriti 3,248 undi, sekali gus membolehkan BN mengekalkan kubu kuat Umno itu dengan mudah.

dcc4e35ec1949042: BANGKOK: The Bank of Thailand is unlikely to cut interest rates below the current 1% without a major economic shock and expects borrowing costs eventually to move higher as policy normalizes, according to Deputy Governor Piti Disyatat.

The current stance is accommodative and stands apart from tighter monetary settings in many other economies, Piti said in a Bloomberg Television interview Wednesday at the IMF-World Bank annual meetings in Bangkok. Thailand’s below-potential growth and relatively contained inflation justify that divergence, he said.

“Unless a big, big shock hits us, we will not go any lower,” Piti said. The 1% benchmark is historically low for Thailand outside periods of crisis and also low compared with other economies, he said, though the central bank retains room to ease if conditions deteriorate sharply.

Over time, however, rates will need to normalize alongside the economic recovery, with the pace depending on inflation and the baht, Piti said. “It’s definitely higher than now,” he said of a normal policy rate, putting the range at about 1.5%-2%. “Normalization, we can take it at our own pace.”

The comments provide some of the clearest guidance yet on the longer-term direction of Thai monetary policy ahead of the central bank’s next rate decision on Oct. 28. Governor Vitai Ratanakorn said Tuesday there was no urgent need to lower borrowing costs while stressing that future decisions remain data dependent.

The central bank has kept its benchmark rate at 1% for three consecutive meetings. Most economists surveyed by Bloomberg still expect it to remain there through the end of 2027, though forecasters at Standard Chartered Plc and Bank of America Corp. have highlighted growing risks to that view.

Thailand faces competing pressures. Inflation accelerated for a second month to 2.82% in September, while sluggish growth and heavy household debt continue to weigh on the economy. The country is also highly exposed to energy shocks, importing about 80% of its crude oil, roughly half of it from the Middle East, according to Piti.

Still, price pressures have been milder than the BOT expected. Piti said full-year inflation will probably be around 2%, below the central bank’s previous 2.8% forecast, while economic growth should be around its earlier 2.3% projection or slightly higher. Updated forecasts will be released with this month’s rate decision.
Recent flooding is also unlikely to materially alter the national outlook, Piti said. While some areas and industries including autos were hit hard, the disruption was localized and is receding.

The central bank also remains comfortable with the baht despite its depreciation this year. Piti said the currency’s resilience through large global shocks reflects confidence in Thailand’s policy framework and economic fundamentals.
Despite slower growth and Thailand’s exposure to the oil shock, “we don’t have the same degree of problems as other countries have had,” Piti said.

f906b803e3fa3d76: Finance Minister Anwar Ibrahim’s Budget 2027 address did not disappoint, transforming fiscal data into an intellectual narrative, and breathing life into the ledger by anchoring it in philosophy.

In tabling the Supply Bill on Oct 9, he assembled a jury of philosophers, poets, and thinkers from five civilisations and asked them to testify. He sought their assistance in telling Malaysians that a budget is not merely arithmetic but a covenant—and that covenants are owed to the future. Everything else in the speech is scaffolding around that claim.
Anwar opened with lighad (“for tomorrow”) from Surah al-Hashr (59:18), establishing intergenerational obligation as a religious duty before it becomes a fiscal one.

He said: “True progress is measured not by how far we travel, but by what we carry together along the way: human dignity, strong families, a fair chance for each generation to rise, the integrity of our institutions, and the conviction that effort will be repaid with opportunity. It is not enough to inherit our strengths. We must enlarge them, until they become a greater legacy for those who follow.”
He then introduced British philosopher Isaiah Berlin’s hedgehog and the fox image: a nation needs "one big thing" held steadily (its ambition) and many things known flexibly (its methods).
“The fox knows many things; the hedgehog knows one big thing. A nation needs both. A nation must hold to one great and constant ambition: a purpose that gives the journey its direction and meaning.”
Immediately after, tenth-century jurist Al-Mawardi established that power cannot stand without order, law, and responsibility.
This was paired with the classical Malay poet Raja Ali Haji’s Gurindam Dua Belas (1847), anchoring the bond between ruler and ruled in waad—a covenant.

“In our tradition, the bond between those who govern and those who are governed has never rested on power alone. It is anchored in waad – a covenant, in which loyalty must be answered with justice, and power must be fenced in by trust.”

The American philosopher John Rawls then performed the heaviest analytical lifting, deploying it at exactly the right moment. After announcing differentiated allocations to states, Anwar anticipated accusations of favouritism and relied on equity rather than uniform treatment:

"That is how we have approached allocations to the states. Developed states can keep surging ahead. Developing states get room to pick up the pace... That is what equity means: not every state getting the same, but every state getting what is fair and reasonable."

Although invoking Rawlsian-adjacent logic provided a philosophical wrapper for inter-governmental distribution, applying it directly glossed over the complex constitutional debates of federal funding formulas. Yet, the rhetoric served its purpose.

Next, Tamil poet-philosopher Thiruvalluvar’s Thirukkural (couplet 731)—which describes a good country as having adequate food production, learned citizens and honest businessmen - arrived just before a RM69 billion education allocation, including RM50 million for Tamil primary schools.
Likewise, a Tang-dynasty monk's verse (Shangtang Kaishi Song) on the plum blossom enduring bitter cold was placed right before fiscal sacrifice and subsidy rationalisation were addressed.
Homer closed the arc. Odysseus braves storms yet never loses his unwavering memory of Ithaca:
"Every nation must know its Ithaca: the ambition it seeks, the values and roots it will defend, and the legacy it means to leave."
Anwar returned to lighad at the close, sealing the ring.

This was no random name-dropping. It was a deliberate comparative theology of governance. Anwar treated the Quran, the Tirukkural, Homer, and Rawls not as conflicting authorities, but as different dialects of the same moral language.

Justice, foresight, and institutional integrity were framed not as Western, Islamic, Indian, Chinese, or Malay monopolies, but as universal human aspirations - a potent message for a multi-ethnic society.
By framing fiscal decisions through a civilisational lens, Anwar attempted to elevate fiscal discipline from a technical necessity to a moral imperative.

One might be tempted to see this as an effort to depoliticise the budget but that risks oversimplifying domestic realpolitik. Rather than neutralising politics, the rhetoric attempted to reshape the terms of political engagement, lifting the conversation above mere transactional patronage.
Anwar’s rhetoric was undeniably ambitious. He wanted Malaysians to see the budget as the fulfillment of a shared moral contract.
Yet, a tension remains.
The intention is to unify, but the ultimate success depends on whether economic benefits are tangibly felt across all communities.

In the end, this covenant will not be weighed in the Dewan Rakyat, but in the lives of the rakyat. If this pluralist vision translates into equitable prosperity, Anwar’s citations will be remembered as the blueprint for a new Malaysia. If not, they will be seen as just beautiful words without substance.

13096602de9f3aae: From Boo Jia Cher
The chaos at Sepang International Circuit during the Formula 1 weekend was frustrating, but hardly surprising.

Thousands of fans were left stranded. Crowds spilled onto the highway, with some fans walking along emergency lanes towards Kuala Lumpur International Airport. Shuttle buses struggled to cope with the sudden surge, while traffic around the circuit ground to a standstill.
It would be easy to dismiss this as a one-off failure of event management. But for anyone who uses Malaysian public transport every day, the problems at Sepang should look very familiar.
Sepang was simply a much bigger, more visible version of the transport problems we already face in our cities.
We still don't take buses seriously
At the heart of the problem is a basic mistake in how we design our roads: buses are still treated as a mode of transport that has to squeeze into traffic, rather than being given priority.
Whenever a major event is expected to attract large crowds, the usual solution is simple: add more buses.

However, putting more buses onto the same congested roads does not solve much. A bus is only useful if it can actually move. A 12-metre bus carrying 50 or 60 people has little advantage over dozens of cars if it is stuck in the same traffic.
That is what happened at Sepang. Once the roads around the circuit became jammed, the shuttle buses could not bypass the congestion. They became part of it.

If a bus that normally takes 20 minutes to complete a trip takes two hours instead, the number of passengers it can carry over the course of the day collapses. Adding more buses only helps if there is enough road capacity for them to move.

This is the same problem commuters face every morning on roads such as Jalan Ampang and the Federal Highway. You can see buses sitting in the same three-lane traffic jam as everyone else while carrying dozens of passengers who chose public transport to avoid sitting in traffic.

A bus carrying 50 people should not have to compete for road space with 50 separate cars. If we want buses to work, they need dedicated, physically protected bus lanes that cannot simply become another lane for cars whenever traffic gets bad.
Grab is not mass transit

Another problem is the tendency to lump taxis and e-hailing services such as Grab into the same category as public transport. They are useful, of course. But they are not a substitute for mass transit.

A Grab car still occupies roughly the same road space as any other car. And when tens of thousands of people leave an event at roughly the same time, asking each person to book an individual car creates an enormous amount of traffic.
Cars have to queue to pick people up, stop at roadsides, make U-turns and squeeze through already crowded roads.

One bus can carry dozens of people in a single vehicle. To move the same number of passengers using individual cars requires a long line of vehicles. That difference matters enormously when road space is limited.

Instead of using e-hailing as a substitute for public transport, planners should treat it as a feeder service that helps people get to rail stations and bus hubs, rather than something that replaces high-capacity transport altogether. Otherwise, we end up filling our roads with hundreds of low-capacity vehicles precisely when we need to move the most people.
The problem doesn't stop at Sepang
There is another problem that is easier to miss. Where do all those extra buses and drivers come from?

In an already underserved public transport system, buses and drivers have to be pulled from regular routes to serve major events. That means someone elsewhere can end up waiting longer for a bus simply because another part of the country is hosting a major event.

This is a sign of how little spare capacity our bus networks have. A healthy public transport system should have enough buses and drivers to handle a major event without effectively robbing one to pay another.
A weekend transport surge can put pressure on ordinary commuters in surrounding neighbourhoods. People who had nothing to do with the event can end up paying for it through longer waiting times.
Johor Bahru should take note

Sepang should also be a warning for Johor Bahru. The upcoming RTS Link will bring large numbers of passengers directly into Bukit Chagar and central Johor Bahru. The rail connection itself is a major and potentially transformative investment.
However, trains do not exist in isolation. What happens after passengers leave the station matters just as much.

If thousands of commuters step out from the Bukit Chagar station and find themselves surrounded by cars, taxis and e-hailing vehicles fighting for space on already congested roads, we could end up recreating the same problem as Sepang, but every day.

Johor Bahru also has a basic problem with walkability. Walking between Bukit Chagar and nearby parts of the city can still mean dealing with broken pavements, a lack of shade, missing crossings and wide, intimidating roads.

A person should not need a car just to cross the street or walk a few hundred metres from a train station. If walking is unpleasant and buses are stuck in traffic, many people will simply choose to drive or book a Grab instead. That adds even more cars to the streets around the station.

The RTS can bring huge numbers of people into the city, but the city still needs to give those people somewhere to go. That means proper pedestrian connections, safe crossings, shaded walkways and dedicated bus lanes should be treated as part of the RTS investment, not as optional improvements to be dealt with later.
We cannot traffic-manage our way out of this

The response to the Sepang chaos focused heavily on traffic police, lane diversions and managing the flow of vehicles. Those things have their place, but they cannot solve a more fundamental problem: too many people are being asked to use the same limited road space at the same time.

We need to start designing our roads around how many people they can move, rather than how many cars they can accommodate. That means giving buses and other high-capacity vehicles priority on dedicated lanes.

It means managing e-hailing pick-up points so they do not clog the entrances to major transport hubs. Major events should also have enough dedicated transport capacity without stripping ordinary neighbourhood bus routes, while walking and cycling should be made a realistic part of the journey, especially around major train stations.

For one weekend, Sepang gave us an unusually clear view of a problem that normally plays out more quietly across Malaysian cities: we built our roads around cars, then expected public transport to somehow work within them.
The lesson from Sepang will keep repeating itself on our highways, outside our train stations, and on the daily commute home, as long as we don't fundamentally change our transport planning.
Boo Jia Cher is an FMT reader.
